What I do 01 — 06

## AI implementation, *grounded in business reality.*

Most AI initiatives fail because they start with the technology instead of the process. I start with your P&L, your workflows and your constraints — then bring AI to where it actually moves the number.

**Direct answer.** AI for business in India, as I practise it, means putting a working system into one owned workflow, with a human review gate. For CA firms, that starts with an AI opportunity audit: a fixed-fee two-week sprint that maps delivery work, scores use cases and leaves a 90-day roadmap. Details are on the [Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit) page and the [CA firms guide](https://pratikbajoria.com/ai-opportunity-audit-for-ca-firms).

01 / STRATEGY

### AI Opportunity Audit

A structured diagnostic of your operations to find where AI delivers measurable ROI — and where it does not.

- Process & workflow mapping
- Use-case scoring by ROI and effort
- Build vs. buy vs. wait analysis
- Prioritised 90-day roadmap

[View package →](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit)

02 / BUILD

### Workflow Automation

Production-grade AI systems built on your existing stack — deployed, tested and handed over with documentation your team can maintain.

- Document & data processing agents
- WhatsApp and email automation
- CRM, ERP and finance integrations
- Internal copilots and assistants

03 / FINANCE

### Finance & Compliance AI

AI applied to the finance function by someone who has actually run it.

- Reconciliation and close automation
- GST, TDS and compliance workflows
- MIS and management reporting
- Audit-ready process controls

04 / ENABLE

### Team Enablement

Adoption is the real bottleneck. I train your people to use AI confidently and correctly, with guardrails that hold up under scrutiny.

- Executive and team workshops
- Prompt libraries and SOPs
- Internal AI usage policy
- Ongoing advisory retainer

05 / SCALE

### Fractional AI Leadership

Senior AI ownership without a senior hire — I sit alongside your leadership team and drive the roadmap to completion.

- Roadmap ownership and governance
- Vendor and tooling selection
- Cost and performance monitoring
- Board and investor reporting

06 / PRODUCT

### AI Product Advisory

For founders embedding AI into what they sell — architecture, positioning and go-to-market, informed by building my own AI product.

- Product architecture review
- Model and infrastructure choices
- Pricing and packaging strategy
- GTM and distribution design

How we work A — D

## From ambiguity *to shipped.*

A deliberately unglamorous four-stage engagement. No pilots that never leave the lab, no decks that gather dust.

STEP 01

### Diagnose

Two weeks inside your operations. I map workflows, interview your team and quantify where time and margin are leaking.

STEP 02

### Prioritise

Every candidate use case scored on business impact, implementation effort and risk. You get a ranked roadmap, not a wish list.

STEP 03

### Build

We ship the highest-value use case first, in weeks rather than quarters. Real system, real users, real measurement.

STEP 04

### Embed

Training, documentation and handover so the capability outlives the engagement. Optional retainer for the next horizon.

AI implementation isn’t sector-agnostic. These are the industries where my finance background and process expertise translate into faster, safer deployments.

CA firms, consultancies and advisory practices looking to scale delivery without scaling headcount.

**Typical build:** invoice processing, vendor reconciliation, MIS reporting

**Typical build:** support automation, catalogue ops, demand insights

**🏥**

**Typical build:** records digitisation, appointment agents, billing workflows

**🏗️**

Developers and brokerages managing long sales cycles, heavy documentation and fragmented lead flow.

**Typical build:** lead qualification, document review, compliance tracking

**⚖️**

In-house legal and compliance functions handling high-volume contract and regulatory review.

**Typical build:** contract review, policy Q&A, obligation tracking

**🚀**

### SaaS & Technology

Founders embedding AI into the product itself, and tech teams needing senior AI direction.

**Typical build:** product AI architecture, internal copilots, GTM strategy

About

## Chartered Accountant. *AI practitioner.*

I’m Pratik Bajoria — a Chartered Accountant with over nine years of post-qualification experience across audit, financial analysis, taxation and business process transformation. Part of that career was spent at a Big-4 firm; the rest across industry roles and, latterly, building my own ventures.

The Big-4 years taught me something most AI consultants never learn: how enterprise processes actually behave under pressure. Materiality thresholds. Control environments. Why a workflow that looks inefficient on paper often exists for a very good reason. The years since — in operating roles and as a founder — taught me the other half: how to actually ship something inside a business that has limited budget and no patience for theory.

My advantage isn’t that I understand AI. Plenty of people do. It’s that I spent nearly a decade inside the finance and operations functions AI is meant to transform, so I can tell a genuine opportunity from an expensive distraction before you commit budget to it.

Today my main work is advising CA firms and companies in India on AI implementation, alongside building **Findost**, my AI-powered wealth management platform. Everything I recommend to clients, I have shipped myself.

I also make a small number of [cross-border introductions](https://crossborder.pratikbajoria.com/) — connecting Indian businesses with international clients and buyers, and overseas companies with vetted Indian partners. Same lens, different problem: I vet both sides the way I would review a counterparty, and I am paid only if a deal closes.

# AI Opportunity Audit for business workflows across teams.

> A fixed-fee, two-week AI opportunity audit for business teams and CA firms in India. Map workflows, score use cases by value and risk, and leave with a prioritised 90-day roadmap.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/audit
Last updated: 2026-11-11

Productised engagement · 2 weeks

An AI opportunity audit, run by a Chartered Accountant in Kolkata: a fixed-fee, two-week sprint that maps workflows, scores use cases, and leaves a prioritised 90-day roadmap. It is built for business teams and for CA firms in India that want throughput gains without weakening review controls.

**Direct answer.** An AI opportunity audit is a fixed-fee, two-week review, led by a Chartered Accountant in Kolkata, of where AI can save time or reduce errors. It maps the work, scores use cases, and leaves a prioritised 90-day roadmap. An AI opportunity audit for CA firms in India applies the same method to delivery and back-office work with review gates.

For the CA-firm walkthrough, including who it is for and how the two weeks run, read the [AI Opportunity Audit for CA firms](https://pratikbajoria.com/ai-opportunity-audit-for-ca-firms).

Fit check 01

## Who is the AI opportunity audit *for?*

### For

- CFOs, COOs and operators who need a ranked list of AI bets, not a tool tour
- Finance and ops leaders under pressure to cut cycle time or error without adding headcount
- Founders who have tried “AI pilots” and want a P&L-grounded next step
- Teams ready to assign an owner and measure outcomes in 90 days

### Not for

- Shopping for a generic chatbot demo or slide deck
- Teams unwilling to share real workflows, volumes or constraints
- Engagements that need a multi-month strategy study before any decision
- Buyers looking for the cheapest tool recommendation without process ownership

Deliverables 02

## What does the AI opportunity audit *include?*

Everything you need to decide where to invest — and where to wait — without inventing a second programme of work.

01 / MAPPING

### Process & workflow mapping

Walk through the high-friction processes that actually burn time and margin. Document owners, systems, volumes and control points.

02 / SCORING

### Use-case scoring

Score candidates on business impact, implementation effort and risk — so “interesting” does not outrank “measurable”.

03 / DECISIONS

### Build / buy / wait

Clear recommendations per use case: build in-house, buy a tool, or wait until data, ownership or process maturity catches up.

04 / ROADMAP

### Prioritised 90-day roadmap

A sequenced plan for the first quarter: what ships first, who owns it, what “done” looks like in numbers.

How it works A — D

## How long does the AI opportunity audit *take?*

The Audit is the Diagnose stage of the wider engagement model — compressed into a fixed sprint so you leave with decisions, not homework.

WEEK 1

### Map

Kick-off, stakeholder interviews and workflow walkthroughs. Surfaces where time and margin leak under real constraints.

WEEK 1–2

### Score

Candidate use cases scored on impact, effort and risk. Weak ideas are cut early — before they consume budget.

WEEK 2

### Decide

Build vs buy vs wait for each priority. Tooling only enters the conversation after the process decision is clear.

DAY 10–14

### Roadmap

Read-out with a prioritised 90-day plan, owners and measurement. Ready for implementation or a pause with eyes open.

Why a diagnostic first Why

## Fund the first win, *not the fifth pilot.*

Most leaders I speak to are not short of AI ideas. They are short of a defensible answer to a simpler question: which one should we fund first, and how will we know it worked? Without that answer, the default is a pilot chosen by whoever saw the best demo.

The numbers say that default is expensive. Gartner predicted that [at least 30% of generative AI projects would be abandoned after proof of concept by the end of 2025](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2024-07-29-gartner-predicts-30-percent-of-generative-ai-projects-will-be-abandoned-after-proof-of-concept-by-end-of-2025), citing poor data quality, inadequate risk controls, escalating costs or unclear business value. McKinsey’s 2026 global survey found that [only 37% of respondents attribute any EBIT impact to AI, a share unchanged from 2025](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai), even though nearly nine in ten use it regularly. Finance is no exception: Gartner’s 2025 survey found [59% of finance leaders using AI, but 91% reporting only low or moderate impact at first](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-18-gartner-survey-shows-finance-ai-adoption-remains-steady-in-2025).

The Audit exists to close that gap before money is committed. As a Chartered Accountant, I treat it the way I would treat any investment decision: baseline first, controls designed in, and a written reason to build, buy or wait.

Investment 03

## Fixed-fee. *Confirmed on the call.*

Pricing

### Fixed-fee two-week sprint — quote confirmed on the discovery call

Scope, access and sector complexity determine the fee. No invented day rates on this page. Book a short discovery call and you leave with a clear quote — or a polite no-fit.

Method

## How the AI opportunity audit *actually runs.*

This is the method in full, so you can judge it before we speak — or run a version yourself. The two-week sprint covers mapping and scoring; the roadmap it leaves takes you to a working release by day 90.

### From two-week audit to a 90-day roadmap

**Days 1–20: map the work.** Pick the five to eight recurring workflows that consume the most skilled time or create the most rework. For each, write five lines: input, decision, output, owner, and what “good” looks like today. In a CA practice this is usually research and first drafts, document extraction, reconciliations, reporting packs and routine client communication. In a finance team it is close, payables, collections and management reporting.

**Days 21–45: score and cut.** Score each workflow on value (hours, cycle time, error cost, cash timing), feasibility (data availability, system access, process stability) and control risk (confidentiality, regulatory exposure, whether an error reaches a client or a filing). Be ruthless. Anything that needs clean data you do not have goes to the “later” column. Anything that would put an unreviewed answer in front of a client goes to “redesign”.

**Days 46–70: design one release.** Take the top one — occasionally two — and design the thin version: which team, which data classes the tool may see, where the human approval gate sits, what is logged, and the metric you will review weekly. Write the stop conditions now, while nobody is emotionally invested.

**Days 71–90: run it beside the old process.** Two to four weeks with one team, reviewed weekly. The output of the audit is not the deck. It is a working release with evidence, or a clean “no” with reasons.

### The plan on one page

90-day AI opportunity audit: phases, outputs and decision gates

| Days | Work | Output | Decision gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1–20 | Map five to eight recurring workflows: input, decision, output, owner, today’s “good” | Workflow maps and a rough baseline | Do we have owners and data for at least three workflows? |
| 21–45 | Score value, feasibility and control risk; cut weekly | Ranked shortlist, with a “later” and a “redesign” column | Which one workflow (occasionally two) goes forward? |
| 46–70 | Design the thin release: team, data classes, human gate, logging, metric, stop conditions | Release design and pilot charter | Is the control design acceptable to the partner, CFO or risk owner? |
| 71–90 | Run beside the old process with one team; weekly review of the exception log | Evidence against the baseline | Keep, change or stop, in writing |

### The scoring rubric

Score each workflow from 1 to 5 on each line. This is a framework for your own data, not benchmark data.

AI opportunity scoring rubric (score your own workflows)

| Dimension | What a 5 looks like | What a 1 looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Value: hours | Many skilled hours every week across the team | A few hours a quarter |
| Value: error and cash | Errors are costly, or cash timing improves | Little cost to an error; no cash effect |
| Feasibility: data | Structured data you already hold and can access | Data is on paper, scattered or owned by a third party |
| Feasibility: process | Stable, written-down steps | Changes every month or lives in one person’s head |
| Control risk (reverse-scored) | Errors are caught inside the business before anyone relies on them | An unreviewed error could reach a client, a filing or a regulator |
| Ownership | A named manager wants it fixed and will run the release | Nobody’s job |

### How to spot audit theatre early

Three signals tell me an audit is drifting. First, the idea list keeps growing after week three; a healthy audit shrinks its list every week. Second, nobody has asked for a baseline — not a perfect cost model, just rough volume, hours by role and the errors people already complain about. Third, the recommendations name tools before they name owners. If a recommendation cannot say who will be accountable for the metric, it is a brochure, not a plan.

Audit theatre versus a useful audit

|   | Theatre | Useful |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starting point | Workshops and a long idea list | Five to eight recurring workflows with owners |
| Baseline | None, or a vendor’s benchmark | Rough volume, hours by role and known error patterns from your own data |
| Idea list over time | Grows every week | Shrinks every week |
| Recommendations | Name tools and platforms | Name owners, metrics and controls first |
| Output | A closing deck | One working release with evidence, or a clean “no” with reasons |

### Governance anchors to use in India

You do not need a heavy framework, but you should be able to show that the audit considered risk in a recognised way. These are the ones I use, depending on the organisation:

- **Any organisation:** the [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) (govern, map, measure, manage) as a neutral checklist.
- **Indian policy direction:** MeitY’s [India AI Governance Guidelines](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2186639) (November 2025), which take a principles-based approach built on existing laws.
- **Personal data:** the [DPDP Rules, 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2190014), notified in November 2025 with an 18-month phased compliance timeline.
- **Regulated financial entities:** the RBI’s [FREE-AI committee report](https://rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=61018) (August 2025), with 7 sutras and 26 recommendations across six pillars.
- **Audit firms:** NFRA’s [General Principles for Technology Adoption in Audit](https://nfra.gov.in/staff-series-on-technology-in-audit/) (July 2026), including validation of tools before live use.

Treat all of them as prompts. Your chart of accounts, staffing and auditor’s expectations are the real constraints.

### Deliverables checklist

- Workflow maps (five lines each) for every workflow reviewed.
- Baseline sheet: volume, hours by role, error patterns, with how each was measured.
- Scored and ranked list, including what was cut and why.
- One release design: team, data classes, human approval gate, logging, metric, stop conditions.
- Cost of the next 90 days, including review time and change management, not just licences.
- Control notes: data protection, who reviews what, and for CA firms, which outputs a signing professional must see.
- Evidence from the parallel run and a written keep, change or stop decision.

### Monday-morning checklist

- List no more than eight recurring workflows and write the five-line map for each.
- Collect a rough baseline: volume, hours by role, known error patterns.
- Score value, feasibility and control risk; cut the list every week.
- Design one thin release with owner, data classes, human gate and stop conditions.
- Judge the audit by the release it ships, not by the length of the deck.

### Frequently asked questions

### What is an AI opportunity audit?

A time-boxed review that maps an organisation’s recurring workflows, scores each on value, feasibility and control risk, and ends with one designed release run beside the existing process, rather than a list of ideas.

### How long does an AI opportunity audit take?

About 90 days if it includes a real parallel run: roughly 20 days to map workflows, 25 to score and cut, 25 to design one release and 20 to run it beside the old process.

### What should an AI audit report contain?

Workflow maps, a baseline, the scored and ranked list with what was cut, one release design with owner, metric and controls, the cost of the next 90 days and, after the parallel run, a written keep, change or stop decision.

### Which frameworks should an AI audit in India refer to?

The NIST AI Risk Management Framework as a neutral checklist, MeitY’s India AI Governance Guidelines, the DPDP Rules, 2025 for personal data, the RBI’s FREE-AI report for regulated financial entities and NFRA’s 2026 principles for audit firms.

### Is an AI audit worth it for a CA firm?

It is worth it when partners want a defensible answer about where AI pays back. For CA firms the audit should also record which outputs a signing professional must review, because AI does not change who is accountable.

FAQ 04

## Questions before *you book.*

### What is an AI Opportunity Audit?

An AI Opportunity Audit is a fixed-fee, two-week diagnostic that maps workflows, scores AI use cases on impact, effort and risk, and delivers a prioritised 90-day roadmap before a build is funded.

### What do you need from us?

Access to process owners, a shortlist of workflows under pressure, and honest volume/cycle-time context. You do not need a polished data lake — you need clarity on how work actually runs.

### Is this a tool selection exercise?

No. Tools come after process and ownership. The Audit decides whether to build, buy or wait — then names the next step.

### What happens after the two weeks?

You leave with a scored roadmap. Many clients continue into implementation or team enablement; some execute internally. Either path is fine if the prioritisation is clear.

### Can this stay remote?

Yes. Remote interviews and screen-shares work well. On-site days can be scoped when the process is heavily paper- or floor-based.

### How do I start?

Book a discovery call, or message on WhatsApp mentioning the Audit. Expect a reply within one business day.

### What is an AI opportunity audit for CA firms in India?

An AI opportunity audit for CA firms in India is a fixed-fee, two-week diagnostic, led by a Chartered Accountant in Kolkata, that maps delivery and back-office workflows, scores use cases against review gates and client-data risk, and leaves a prioritised 90-day roadmap. The CA-firm walkthrough is on the [Audit for CA firms](https://pratikbajoria.com/ai-opportunity-audit-for-ca-firms) page.

### How long does the AI opportunity audit take?

The diagnostic itself is a fixed two-week sprint. The roadmap it leaves is designed so one first release can run, beside the old process, by day 90. The fee is confirmed on the discovery call; there is no published list price on this page.

# AI Opportunity Scorecard.

> Free AI Opportunity Scorecard for CFOs and operators — score process, data, ROI, risk and ownership before you spend on AI.

Last updated: 2026-11-11

Lead magnet · Free

A practical checklist for CFOs and operators. Score yourself across process, data, ROI, risk and ownership — before you fund another pilot that goes nowhere.

**Direct answer.** The AI Opportunity Scorecard is a free checklist for CFOs, operators and CA-firm partners. It scores process readiness, data quality, likely return, risk and ownership before you fund an AI pilot. Enter a work email to unlock the full list. If the gaps are in ownership or data, fix those first; if scores are strong, the next step is the [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit).

## Email to unlock.

Why score first Why

## Ten minutes now, *not a wasted quarter.*

The scorecard exists because most AI proposals arrive with a tool attached and the hard questions missing. Who owns the workflow? What does it cost today? What data will the tool see, and who checks the output? If those answers are blank, the score will show it, and that is cheaper to learn now than after a renewal.

Those gaps are common. Gartner predicted that [at least 30% of generative AI projects would be abandoned after proof of concept by the end of 2025](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2024-07-29-gartner-predicts-30-percent-of-generative-ai-projects-will-be-abandoned-after-proof-of-concept-by-end-of-2025), with unclear business value and weak risk controls among the reasons. Use is also running ahead of design: in Microsoft and LinkedIn's 2024 Work Trend Index, [75% of knowledge workers said they use generative AI at work, and 78% of those users bring their own tools](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2024/05/08/microsoft-and-linkedin-release-the-2024-work-trend-index-on-the-state-of-ai-at-work/). And McKinsey's 2025 survey found [only about a third of organisations have begun to scale AI](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai), even though most use it somewhere.

Score honestly. A low score on ownership or data is not a failure; it is the most useful result the checklist can give you.

# Unlock cash and make the next move.

> Practical MSME support for overdue receivables, scheme discovery, debt readiness, excess inventory and tender opportunities. Scope and outcomes are confirmed case by case.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/msme-services

For Indian MSMEs · Practical commercial support

Focused support for five recurring business challenges: overdue customer payments, finding relevant schemes, preparing for debt conversations, moving excess stock and identifying suitable tenders. Start with the problem; agree a specific scope before any work begins.

**Clear scope, no outcome promises.** Scheme eligibility, payment recovery, buyer interest and tender awards depend on facts and third-party decisions. Specialist or regulated work is referred to the appropriately qualified provider and identified before engagement.

Five MSME service areas 01 — 05

## Work on the commercial *constraint in front of you.*

A focused engagement can address one priority or combine related work. We first establish the facts, decision owner and desired outcome, then confirm a practical plan.

01 / CASH FLOW

### Receivables recovery support

Organise overdue receivables and supporting records so your team can pursue clear, well-evidenced follow-up.

- Review ageing, customer concentration and dispute status.
- Match invoices with purchase orders and delivery evidence.
- Prioritise follow-up and prepare approved reconciliation reminders.
- Coordinate application documentation for potentially eligible routes; legal escalation remains with qualified counsel.

02 / SCHEMES

### Subsidy and incentive discovery

Screen potentially relevant central and state programs against your location, sector, project and current official criteria.

- Build a business profile and scheme shortlist.
- Check published eligibility conditions and application windows.
- Prepare a document checklist and application drafts.
- Track follow-up items; eligibility and approval are determined by the scheme authority.

03 / FINANCE

### Debt readiness and financial strategy

Turn business records into management questions and a clearer financing conversation, based on the engagement scope.

- Review cash conversion, receivables, payables and working-capital needs.
- Assess product or customer contribution where reliable data allows.
- Prepare cash-flow scenarios and debt-service discussion points.
- Organise lender-ready information; this is advisory support, not lending or credit approval.

04 / INVENTORY

### Excess inventory buyer matching

Help make slow-moving, surplus or eligible second-grade inventory easier for prospective buyers to evaluate.

- Structure stock details by quantity, age, condition and location.
- Prepare a buyer-ready catalogue and indicative asking information.
- Identify and approach relevant buyer categories with your approval.
- Commercial terms, inspection, quality, payment and logistics are agreed by the transacting parties.

05 / PUBLIC PROCUREMENT

### Tender intelligence and bid support

Focus your team on opportunities that appear to fit your products, credentials, capacity and delivery geography.

- Shortlist opportunities from relevant authorized sources.
- Summarise eligibility, deadlines and required documents.
- Review document gaps and support bid preparation and pricing inputs.
- Submission requires your approval; selection remains with the procuring authority.

**Engagement boundaries:** Work starts only after the parties agree deliverables, access to information, provider responsibilities and fees in writing. Do not share sensitive financial, customer or identity data through an initial enquiry.

How an engagement starts 02

## From business issue *to an agreed action plan.*

STEP 01

### Explain the situation

Share your sector, state, business stage and the commercial issue in broad terms. No confidential documents are needed for the first conversation.

STEP 02

### Confirm fit and scope

Identify what can be supported, what evidence is needed, who is responsible and which specialist providers may be required.

STEP 03

### Agree and proceed

Confirm deliverables, fees, data handling, dependencies and decision points in writing before work begins.

Common questions 03

## Know the limits *before you commit.*

### Do you guarantee recovery, subsidy approval or a tender award?

No. These outcomes depend on the evidence, eligibility, counterparty or authority decisions, and competition. The work is scoped around preparation and support, without promising a result.

### Do you provide loans or guarantee credit?

No. This is not a lending service and does not guarantee financing. Debt-readiness support can help organise your business information and prepare questions for lenders; the lender independently decides whether to offer credit.

### Can you handle legal notices or represent us in a dispute?

Legal representation and reserved legal work must be handled by appropriately qualified legal professionals. Where relevant, the engagement can focus on organising business records and coordinating with your chosen counsel.

### Can the service be customized to my industry and state?

Yes. The scope can be tailored to your business, location, records, timeline and priority. Scheme screening uses current published criteria available for the specific program, and requires case-by-case confirmation.

### How are fees decided?

Fees depend on the agreed scope, deliverables, effort and any disclosed specialist-provider involvement. They are confirmed in writing before work begins; this page does not quote or imply a standard fee.

### What should I include in the first enquiry?

Share your sector, state, approximate business stage and a short description of the requirement. Please do not attach bank statements, customer records, identity documents or other sensitive information until a secure process has been agreed.

# Startup operations, from setup to scale.

> Startup operations support tailored to your stage, city and budget: workspace search, business operations, finance workflows and AI automation, with partner scope made clear.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/startup-operations
Last updated: 2026-11-01

For founders · Tailored operating support

One coordinated plan for the work behind a growing business: workspace, essential services, finance operations and practical automation—shaped around your stage, city and budget.

**Direct answer.** Pratik works with founders to scope startup operating needs, directly leading workflow discovery and automation. Workspace, legal, hiring, branding and specialist IT work is coordinated with the relevant providers, with availability, responsibilities and fees confirmed before you commit.

What we can coordinate 01 — 04

## Build the operating base *your startup needs now.*

Choose the immediate bottleneck first. The scope can combine direct workflow work with specialist services where needed; every provider’s role is made clear in the plan.

01 / WORKSPACE

### Find a workable place to operate

Define location, capacity, term and budget, then explore coworking, private-office or managed-space options. Availability and commercial terms are checked with the provider before you decide.

02 / BUSINESS FOUNDATIONS

### Coordinate the services around launch

Map the setup tasks and connect with relevant accounting, tax, legal, incorporation, hiring or IT specialists. Regulated or specialist work is handled by the appropriate provider under a clearly agreed scope.

03 / OPERATING WORKFLOWS

### Make day-to-day work easier to run

Clarify ownership and hand-offs across customer onboarding, sales follow-up, support, procurement, reporting and finance operations. Document how work happens before choosing tools.

04 / AUTOMATION

### Automate the right repeatable steps

Design and implement workflow automation across business functions, connecting the tools you already use where practical. Keep human review for exceptions, sensitive decisions and approvals.

**Delivery clarity:** Process discovery and workflow automation are led directly by Pratik. Other services can be coordinated with your existing providers or relevant specialists. Provider availability, fees, referral arrangements and responsibilities are disclosed and agreed before work starts.

A tailored engagement 02

## Start with your stage *and the job to be done.*

A pre-launch founder may need workspace and setup coordination. A team already trading may need cleaner hand-offs, reliable finance workflows or automation. We scope the work to your actual priorities.

STEP 01

### Share the brief

Tell me your stage, city, team size, budget range, timeline and the one or two issues you need solved first.

STEP 02

### Agree the plan

We map the requirements, separate direct delivery from provider work, and confirm deliverables, owners, fees and dependencies.

STEP 03

### Coordinate and improve

Work through the agreed priorities, track open decisions and adjust the next steps as the startup’s needs change.

Fit check 03

## Useful when operations *are slowing the founder down.*

### A good starting point

- You are launching or growing a business and need a clear order of operations.
- You want workspace and business services considered alongside the operating plan.
- Manual hand-offs across sales, customer support, finance or operations are consuming time.
- You prefer to understand provider scope and costs before making commitments.

### What to bring to the first conversation

- Startup stage and target city or workspace area.
- Team size, budget range and desired timeline.
- The services you already have and the gaps you need to fill.
- A recent example of a task or hand-off that is creating friction.

Common questions 04

## Know who does what *before you begin.*

### What does startup operations support include?

The scope is customized. It can include workspace search, coordination with specialist business-service providers, finance and operating workflows, and AI-enabled process automation. The plan identifies who delivers each item and what it costs.

### Does Pratik personally deliver every service?

Pratik directly leads process discovery, operating workflow design and automation work. Workspace, legal, entity, hiring, branding or specialist IT services are coordinated with the relevant provider. The provider, responsibilities and fees are agreed before work begins.

### Can the plan be tailored to our startup?

Yes. The recommended scope depends on your startup stage, city, team size, budget, priorities and timeline. Share those details during an introductory conversation.

### Can you arrange office space in any city?

Workspace options depend on the requested city, budget, size and current provider availability. Availability and commercial terms are confirmed before you make a decision.

### How are fees handled when a specialist provider is involved?

The written scope should identify each provider, their deliverable and fee, and any referral or coordination fee before the engagement starts.

I’m a Chartered Accountant based in Kolkata, with over nine years of post-qualification experience across audit, financial analysis, taxation and business process transformation. Part of that time was spent at a Big 4 firm. The rest has been in industry roles and, more recently, building my own ventures.

Audit work is where I learnt how finance processes behave when a deadline is close and the numbers have to tie. I saw why a step that looks wasteful on paper is often there for a reason, usually a control someone needed after something went wrong. That shapes how I look at AI now. Before I suggest automating a workflow, I want to know which control it carries and who signs off on the output.

# AI Automation in India: A Practical Hub for Business Owners

> AI automation in India for owners and operations heads: which workflows to automate first, DPDP and RBI considerations, human review and a 90-day plan.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/ai-automation-in-india
Last updated: 2026-11-11

AI automation · Updated 11 November 2026 · 7 min read

Where AI automation actually pays back for Indian businesses, what the DPDP Act and sector regulators expect, and how to run a first project without losing control of the work.

**Direct answer.** AI automation in India, as I use the term, means putting AI inside one owned business workflow (a customer message, a document, a reconciliation exception or a recurring report) so the routine part runs faster while a named person still owns the result. For CA practices, the parallel guide is [AI for Chartered Accountants in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-for-chartered-accountants-in-india).

Most conversations I have about “AI automation in India” start with a tool and end with a pilot nobody uses. The businesses that get value tend to do it the other way round. They pick one workflow that already hurts, write down who owns it and what good looks like, and only then decide what to automate. I am a chartered accountant and worked at a Big 4 firm before founding Findost, so I come at this from the controls side: if you cannot explain the output to an auditor, a customer or a regulator, it is not ready.

This page is the index for everything I have written on automation outside the CA practice itself: sales and customer workflows, operations, governance and tooling. For the profession-specific guides, see [AI for chartered accountants in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-for-chartered-accountants-in-india); for close, reconciliation and ROI, see [AI implementation for finance teams](https://pratikbajoria.com/ai-implementation-for-finance-teams).

## What AI automation should mean for an Indian business

Useful automation is narrow and checkable. In practice that usually means one of five jobs:

- **Enquiries and customer messages:** sorting and drafting first replies on WhatsApp and email, with a person approving anything that commits the business.
- **Documents:** pulling fields out of invoices, purchase orders, KYC files or property documents and flagging what is missing.
- **Reconciliations and exceptions:** matching marketplace, bank and ledger data and sending only the mismatches to a reviewer.
- **CRM and pipeline hygiene:** logging calls, updating stages and nudging follow-ups so the sales record reflects reality.
- **Recurring reporting:** first drafts of MIS commentary from controlled data, reviewed before anyone sees them.

What these have in common is a defined input, a repeatable transformation and an owner who can judge the result. That is also why finance is often the first function to move: Gartner’s 2025 survey found [59% of finance leaders using AI in their function](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-18-gartner-survey-shows-finance-ai-adoption-remains-steady-in-2025), up from 37% in 2023.

## By the numbers

The scale of the opportunity, and the size of the gap between using AI and getting a return from it. Each figure links to its source and date.

## Why so many automation pilots stall

The pattern is well documented. Gartner predicted that [at least 30% of generative AI projects would be abandoned after proof of concept by the end of 2025](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2024-07-29-gartner-predicts-30-percent-of-generative-ai-projects-will-be-abandoned-after-proof-of-concept-by-end-of-2025), citing poor data quality, weak risk controls, rising costs and unclear business value. In my experience the fix is boring: a baseline taken before the tool arrives, a named owner, a review gate and a weekly metric. I have written that up as [the Monday morning test for any AI workflow](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-29-the-monday-morning-test-for-any-ai-workflow) and in [why most corporate AI pilots never reach production](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/corporate-ai-pilots).

## The Indian rules that shape the design

Two sets of rules come up in almost every Indian automation project.

- **Personal data:** the [Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/Digital-Personal-Data-Protection-Act-2023.pdf) applies to digital personal data of individuals, and the government [notified the DPDP Rules on 14 November 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2190014). Customer chats, KYC files and employee data all count, so map what personal data each workflow uses before it reaches an AI tool.
- **Regulated entities:** if you are a bank, NBFC or other RBI-regulated entity, read the RBI’s [FREE-AI committee report (August 2025)](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/PublicationReportDetails.aspx?ID=1306). Even outside financial services it is a sensible checklist of what a regulator would expect to see written down: a board-approved policy, an inventory of AI uses and an incident process.

For a framework-neutral way to structure the risk work, the [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) is free and practical. None of this is legal advice; confirm your position on your own facts.

AI adoption steps for Indian SMEs, drawn from the WEF, IndiaAI (MeitY) and PSA playbook for India’s SMEs (August 2025). Source: [WEF with IndiaAI and the Office of the PSA: Transforming Small Businesses, an AI Playbook for India’s SMEs](https://www.psa.gov.in/CMS/web/sites/default/files/publication/WEF_Transforming_Small_Businesses_2025.pdf).

### Text version of this infographic

- **Context:** India has more than 60 million MSMEs, contributing about 30% of GDP and about half of exports; only 19% of MSME credit demand is met through formal sources.
- **Step 1, find your data phase:** phase 0 is paper ledgers and manual logs (AI can look back at historical trends); phase 1 is spreadsheets, Tally, Zoho or a basic ERP or CRM (basic trends and automated reporting); phase 2 is APIs, sensors, QR tools and cloud platforms (predictive planning); phase 3 is fully integrated real-time systems (prescriptive, automated workflows).
- **Step 2, score each use case:** impact (business value, strategic alignment, people affected) and feasibility (operational readiness, cost to deploy).
- **Step 3:** start where impact is high and implementation is easy, then add use cases in phases. Microenterprises should begin with free or low-cost tools, AI-as-a-service and mobile apps; 85% of Indians have a mobile phone and 60% have internet access.

## A 90-day sequence that survives contact with the business

1. **Days 1–30:** pick one workflow, record today’s volumes, cycle time and error rate, and decide which steps must stay human.
2. **Days 31–60:** run the automation in parallel with the existing process, with every output reviewed and every exception logged.
3. **Days 61–90:** compare against the baseline and make a written go, adjust or stop decision. Only then widen the scope.

The full version, with an opportunity scoring method, is in [a 90-day AI opportunity audit without the theatre](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit). If you are weighing a custom build against an off-the-shelf tool, read [build vs buy AI tooling](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/build-vs-buy-ai-tooling) first.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is AI for business in India?

AI for business in India, as I practise it, means putting a working system into one owned workflow, with a human review gate. The starting point is a painful, owned process, not a tool shortlist. This hub covers the business-owner path. CA firms should use the [AI for Chartered Accountants in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-for-chartered-accountants-in-india) hub.

### What is AI automation for a business in India?

It is using AI inside a defined workflow, such as reading an invoice, sorting a customer enquiry or flagging a reconciliation exception, so that the routine part runs faster while a named person still owns the result. It is different from simply giving staff a chatbot.

### Which business processes should an Indian company automate with AI first?

Start with work that is repetitive, has a clear input and output, and has an owner who can say what a correct result looks like: enquiry routing on WhatsApp or email, document extraction, reconciliation exceptions, CRM hygiene and recurring MIS drafts. Leave unsupervised advice and anything you cannot check for later.

### Does the DPDP Act affect AI automation?

Yes, if the workflow touches personal data of individuals in India. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules notified in November 2025 set out duties on notice, consent, purpose, security safeguards and breach reporting. Map what personal data a workflow uses before you send it to any AI tool, and take legal advice on your facts.

### How long does a first AI automation project take?

Plan for one workflow over roughly 90 days: a baseline and design in the first month, a supervised parallel run in the second, and a written go, adjust or stop decision in the third. Scope it so it can be measured within a quarter.

# AI implementation for finance teams.

> Where CFOs and controllers should start with AI: month-end close, reconciliations, invoice intake and MIS, with controls, owners and a 90-day roadmap.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/ai-implementation-for-finance-teams
Last updated: 2026-11-11

Guide · CFOs & finance controllers

A direct path for CFOs and controllers who need measurable cycle-time and error-cost wins — without weakening controls, GST/TDS discipline or board-pack integrity.

**Direct answer.** Finance teams should start AI implementation on one high-friction owned workflow — close, reconciliation, invoice intake or MIS — map systems and control points, score use cases on impact and risk, then ship a prioritised 90-day roadmap with review gates. Tool demos come after process ownership. Prefer a free self-check via the [Scorecard](https://pratikbajoria.com/scorecard), a structured [Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit), or [book a discovery call](https://pratikbajoria.com/#contact).

Last updated 11 November 2026 · Written by [CA Pratik Bajoria](https://pratikbajoria.com/about), Chartered Accountant in Kolkata

Why finance first 01

## P&L pressure is already *measurable.*

Close days, reconciliation backlogs, invoice exceptions and MIS turnaround are numbers the CFO already watches. That makes finance a sharper starting point than open-ended “AI exploration”. The constraint is not models — it is ownership, audit trails and deciding what must stay human-signed.

01 / CLOSE

### Month-end pressure

Compress pack preparation and exception queues without removing controller sign-off on the numbers that go to the board.

02 / RECON

### Reconciliation & exceptions

Triage matches and mismatches with human review on material items — cycle time and error cost stay visible.

03 / INTAKE

### Invoice & vendor documents

Extract into ERP or AP flows with logging so GST/TDS and vendor master rules are respected.

04 / MIS

### Reporting with sources

Draft board and MIS packs from controlled sources; finance owns the narrative and the figures.

Fit check 02

## Who this helps *— and who it does not.*

### For

- CFOs and controllers who can name a process, owner and metric
- Finance teams under pressure to cut close or exception cycle time
- Leaders who want AI with review gates, not unsupervised postings
- Teams willing to share real volumes, ERP context and control constraints

### Not for

- Fully autonomous finance advice without human ownership
- Tool shopping without process or volume context
- Projects that need a multi-month strategy study before any decision
- Buyers seeking the cheapest chatbot list with no stop rule

## By the numbers

Where finance teams actually are with AI, from the most recent surveys and official data. Each figure links to its source and date.

59%

of finance leaders report using AI in their finance function (183 CFOs and senior finance leaders surveyed, May–June 2025), against 37% in 2023.

Source: [Gartner, 18 November 2025](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-18-gartner-survey-shows-finance-ai-adoption-remains-steady-in-2025)

49% · 37% · 34%

of finance AI users apply it to knowledge management, accounts payable automation and error or anomaly detection respectively.

Source: [Gartner, 18 November 2025](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-18-gartner-survey-shows-finance-ai-adoption-remains-steady-in-2025)

91%

of finance AI adopters reported low or moderate impact at first; bigger gains came once projects reached production.

FAQ 03

## Questions CFOs *ask before starting.*

### Where should a CFO start with AI implementation?

Start with one finance workflow that already has owners, volumes and a visible metric — month-end close, reconciliation exceptions, invoice intake or MIS packs — then map controls before buying tools.

### Will AI replace finance controls or sign-off?

No. Effective finance AI assists throughput and exception triage while controllers and CFOs keep ownership of postings, filings and board numbers. Review gates and audit trails are designed in, not bolted on later.

### What finance use cases usually win first?

Reconciliation and exception queues with human review, document extraction into ERP or close packs, invoice and vendor-document intake with logging, and MIS or board-pack drafting from controlled sources.

Why CA firms 01

## What is an AI opportunity audit *for CA firms in India?*

Practices sit on document-heavy, deadline-driven work. AI can compress intake, extraction and first-draft research — but only when ownership, review gates and confidentiality are designed in. A generic chatbot pilot rarely survives partner scrutiny; a scored roadmap does.

01 / MAP

### Delivery & back-office mapping

Walk compliance calendars, engagement packs, reconciliation routines and client paperwork with the people who own the work.

02 / SCORE

### Use cases with controls

Score candidates on impact, effort and risk — including review gates, logging and what must remain human-signed.

03 / DECIDE

### Build / buy / wait

Clear calls per use case. Tooling follows process and ownership — not the other way around.

04 / ROADMAP

### 90-day priorities

A sequenced plan for the first quarter: what ships, who owns it, and what “done” looks like in cycle time and error rates.

Fit check 02

## Who is the AI opportunity audit *for?*

### For

- Managing partners and practice leads who need a ranked list of AI bets, not a tool tour
- Firms under pressure to cut pack turnaround or exception queues without adding unchecked headcount
- Teams ready to keep professional judgement with partners while automating throughput
- Practices willing to share real volumes, systems and confidentiality constraints

### Not for

- Shopping for an unsupervised “AI that signs opinions”
- Firms unwilling to discuss client-data handling or review gates
- Engagements that need a multi-month strategy study before any decision
- Buyers seeking the cheapest tool list without process ownership

Typical CA scope A — D

## Which CA firm workflows *are usually in scope?*

INTAKE

### Documents

Extraction into engagement packs and working papers, with human review on exceptions.

COMPLIANCE

### Calendars & filings

Support for deadlines and checklists — not unsupervised filing decisions.

FINANCE OPS

### Reconciliations

Exception handling and pack preparation where cycle time and error cost are visible.

KNOWLEDGE

### Research drafts

Memo and research first drafts with mandatory partner or manager review gates.

Full package details and booking also live on the [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit) page.

Process and timeline 03

## How does the two-week sprint *actually run?*

The diagnostic is two weeks. The roadmap it leaves is built so one first release can run, beside the old process, by day 90. This is the same method as the [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit), written for a CA practice.

DAYS 1–20

### Map the work

Pick the five to eight recurring workflows that consume the most skilled time or create the most rework. In a CA practice this is usually research and first drafts, document extraction, reconciliations, reporting packs and routine client communication. For each, write the input, decision, output, owner, and what “good” looks like today.

DAYS 21–45

### Score and cut

Score each workflow on value (hours, cycle time, error cost), feasibility (data, system access, process stability) and control risk (confidentiality, regulatory exposure, whether an error could reach a client or a filing). Weak ideas go to a later or redesign column.

DAYS 46–70

### Design one release

Take the top one, occasionally two, and design the thin version: which team, which data classes the tool may see, where the human approval gate sits, what is logged, and the metric you will review weekly. Write the stop conditions now.

DAYS 71–90

### Run it beside the old process

Two to four weeks with one team, reviewed weekly. The output of the audit is a working release with evidence, or a clean no with reasons, not a slide deck.

What you leave with: workflow maps and a rough baseline, a ranked shortlist with later and redesign columns, a release design with a human gate and logging, and a written keep, change or stop decision once the first release has run. The fee is confirmed on the discovery call; there is no published list price on this page.

# How to start AI implementation.

> How mid-market and finance teams should start AI implementation: map workflows, score use cases, then ship a prioritised 90-day roadmap — not another pilot.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/how-to-start-ai-implementation
Last updated: 2026-11-11

Guide · Mid-market & finance

A practical sequence for CFOs, COOs and operators who want measurable P&L impact — not another demo that dies in a slide deck.

**Direct answer.** Start by picking one high-friction workflow with clear owners and measurable pain, map it end to end, score candidate use cases on impact and risk, then decide build/buy/wait before you fund a tool. Compress that into a prioritised 90-day roadmap — the same discipline as an [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit).

Last updated 11 November 2026 · Written by [CA Pratik Bajoria](https://pratikbajoria.com/about), Chartered Accountant in Kolkata

Why most starts fail 01

## Tool-first is the *expensive default.*

Mid-market teams often begin with a vendor shortlist or a chatbot pilot. Without process ownership, volume context and a stop rule, pilots linger and never reach production. Finance teams feel this acutely: close, GST/TDS, reconciliation and MIS already have controls that AI must respect — not bypass.

01 / PRESSURE

### Choose a P&L pressure point

Month-end close, vendor reconciliation, invoice intake, exception queues or board reporting. If you cannot name the metric, you are not ready to automate.

02 / MAP

### Map the real workflow

Interview the people who run it. Capture systems, hand-offs, volumes and control points. Spreadsheets and email are part of the process — document them.

03 / SCORE

### Score before you buy

Rank use cases on business impact, effort and risk. Cut weak ideas early so “interesting” does not outrank “measurable”.

04 / DECIDE

### Build, buy or wait

Tooling enters only after process and ownership are clear. Waiting is a valid decision when data or governance is not ready.

Recommended sequence A — E

## Five steps that *actually ship.*

This is the Diagnose → Prioritise path compressed for leaders who need a Monday-morning plan.

STEP 1

### Pressure point

One workflow, one owner, one metric. Prefer finance and ops friction over open-ended research agents.

STEP 2

### Map

Walk the process with operators. Note volumes, cycle times, systems and where errors or rework concentrate.

STEP 3

### Score

Impact × effort × risk. Keep a shortlist of three or fewer for the first quarter.

STEP 4

### Decide

Build, buy or wait per use case. Assign an owner and a definition of done in numbers.

**Step 5 — Roadmap.** Sequence 90 days: what ships first, who owns it, how you measure, and when you stop. Many teams run this as a structured [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit); others execute internally once the prioritisation is clear.

Finance-specific 02

## Where finance teams *usually win first.*

### Strong first bets

- Reconciliation and exception handling with human review
- Document extraction into ERP or close packs
- MIS / board pack drafting with controlled sources
- Invoice and vendor-document intake with audit trails

### Usually wait

- Fully autonomous advice without review gates
- Broad “company chatbot” with no process owner
- Projects that need a multi-month strategy study before any decision
- Tool tours without volume or control context

Prefer a free self-check first? Use the [AI Opportunity Scorecard](https://pratikbajoria.com/scorecard). Ready for a structured two-week diagnostic? See the [Audit package](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit).

FAQ 03

## Questions mid-market *teams ask first.*

### Where should a mid-market finance team start with AI?

Start with one high-friction finance or ops workflow that already has owners and measurable pain — reconciliation, close, invoice processing or MIS — then map it before buying tools.

### Do we need a data lake before AI implementation?

No. You need clarity on how work actually runs: volumes, systems, hand-offs and controls. Many first wins sit on existing ERP, email and spreadsheet flows with light integration.

### What is an AI Opportunity Audit?

A fixed-fee two-week sprint that maps workflows, scores use cases, makes build/buy/wait decisions and delivers a prioritised 90-day roadmap. See the [Audit package](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit).

# Workflow automation with AI for mid-market.

> Workflow automation with AI for mid-market COOs: map hand-offs, pick owned bottlenecks, decide build, buy or wait, and ship automations within 90 days.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/workflow-automation-with-ai-for-mid-market
Last updated: 2026-11-11

Guide · Mid-market ops & COO

A practical playbook for COOs and ops leaders who need production automations on owned bottlenecks — not another pilot that dies in a slide deck.

**Direct answer.** Mid-market workflow automation with AI starts by picking one owned bottleneck with volume, mapping hand-offs and systems end to end, scoring build/buy/wait, then shipping inside a prioritised 90-day roadmap with a stop rule. Skip tool tours without process ownership. Next steps: free [Scorecard](https://pratikbajoria.com/scorecard), structured [Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit), or [contact](https://pratikbajoria.com/#contact).

Why pilots stall 01

## Automation without owners *does not ship.*

Mid-market ops teams often buy a platform or spin up a chatbot before naming the bottleneck. Without volumes, hand-offs and a stop/continue rule, work stays in “pilot”. AI helps when it compresses a real queue — documents, exceptions, routing, CRM/ERP updates — under an accountable owner.

01 / BOTTLENECK

### One owned queue

Lead qualification, document intake, order exceptions, support triage or internal reporting — pick one with a metric.

02 / MAP

### Hand-offs & systems

Walk the process with operators. Capture email, WhatsApp, spreadsheets, CRM and ERP as they actually run.

03 / DECIDE

### Build / buy / wait

Score impact, effort and risk. Tooling follows process clarity — waiting is valid when ownership is missing.

04 / SHIP

### 90-day production

Sequence what goes live first, who owns it, how you measure, and when you stop or expand.

Fit check 02

## Who this helps *— and who it does not.*

### For

- COOs and ops leads who can name a bottleneck, owner and volume
- Mid-market teams ready to ship production automations, not endless demos
- Leaders who want build/buy/wait clarity before funding another tool
- Organisations willing to change hand-offs, not only add software

### Not for

- Company-wide chatbots with no process owner
- Buyers seeking the cheapest automation list without metrics
- Engagements that need a multi-month strategy study before any decision
- Fully unsupervised customer or compliance decisions

INTAKE

### Documents

ROUTING

### WhatsApp & email

Triage and hand-off to the right owner without losing control of the conversation.

EXCEPTIONS

### Queues

Order, support or ops exceptions ranked by materiality so humans focus on what matters.

SYSTEMS

### Light integration

Updates to CRM/ERP and internal MIS once the process and ownership are clear.

### What is workflow automation with AI for mid-market companies?

Using AI and integrations to reduce hand-offs, cycle time and rework on owned operational workflows — document intake, exception queues, WhatsApp/email routing, CRM or ERP updates — with clear owners and stop rules, not unsupervised company-wide chatbots.

### Where should a COO start?

# AI for Virtual CFO Services: MIS Packs Clients Actually Read

> AI makes the monthly MIS pack faster to build. What a virtual CFO adds is the few lines of commentary a partner stands behind. How to build packs clients read.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-11-11-ai-for-virtual-cfo-services-mis-packs-clients-actually-read
Last updated: 2026-11-11

CA insights · 2026-11-11 · 4 min read

Many CA practices now offer virtual CFO services to growing businesses, and the monthly MIS pack is usually the centre of it. Too often it is a long export that the founder opens once, scrolls through and closes. AI can make that pack faster to produce, but speed is not the problem. Relevance is.

This is how I would use AI to build an MIS pack a client actually reads, and keep the partner’s time on the part that matters.

## Start with the three questions the client cares about

Most owner-managed businesses want to know three things every month: how much cash they have and will have, whether they made money, and what needs their attention. Everything else in the pack should support those answers or go into an appendix. I set out the layout I use in [how to build a monthly business dashboard](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/how-to-build-a-monthly-business-dashboard).

- Cash: current balance, the expected position over the next few weeks, and the receivables and payables driving it.
- Profitability: revenue and margin against budget and last year, by the lines the owner actually manages.
- Attention: a short list of items needing a decision, each with a recommended action.

## What AI does well in MIS work

These map closely to the most common finance AI uses in Gartner’s [2025 survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-18-gartner-survey-shows-finance-ai-adoption-remains-steady-in-2025): knowledge management, payables automation and anomaly detection. Gartner also found most teams saw low or moderate impact at first, which is a reminder to start narrow.

- Pulling data from the accounting system, bank feeds and sales tools into a consistent monthly dataset.
- Producing the standard tables and charts in the same format every month.
- Flagging movements above agreed thresholds and drafting a first explanation from the ledger detail.
- Answering the client’s follow-up questions about the numbers from the same dataset.
- Spotting unusual items: new vendors, duplicate payments, sudden changes in customer payment patterns.

## One compliance line every Indian MIS pack should show

If the client buys from micro or small enterprises, payables ageing is not just a cash question. Under [section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006](https://www.dcmsme.gov.in/msmed2006.pdf), the agreed payment period to such suppliers cannot exceed 45 days from acceptance or deemed acceptance, and section 16 makes the buyer liable for compound interest with monthly rests, at three times the bank rate notified by the Reserve Bank, on late payments.

An MIS pack that shows MSME payables approaching 45 days, by supplier, is a practical way to avoid that interest. Supplier classification also needs refreshing: the [Union Budget 2025-26](https://pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2098389) raised the investment and turnover limits for MSME classification by 2.5 and 2 times respectively, so some suppliers will now fall into a different category.

## The commentary is the product

The part of the pack a client values most is the few lines at the top: what happened, why, and what to do. AI can draft those lines from the numbers, and the draft is often a useful start. But only someone who knows the client can say that the margin dip is a new contract’s mobilisation cost and will reverse next quarter, or that it is the start of a pricing problem.

I would make it a rule that the commentary is rewritten and signed off by the partner or senior manager every month. That is where a virtual CFO service earns its fee, and it is the part a tool cannot replace.

## Getting the data plumbing right

The biggest time cost in MIS work is collecting and cleaning data. Consent-based feeds help: the Account Aggregator ecosystem, according to [Sahamati](https://sahamati.org.in/media-article/account-aggregator-crosses-500-million-consents-as-india-marks-5th-aa-foundation-day/), now has more than 1,100 regulated entities live and over 2.8 billion financial accounts enabled for sharing. Where a client’s banks and tools support structured feeds, use them rather than downloaded statements.

- Agree the chart of accounts mapping with the client once, and keep it stable.
- Close the books on a fixed timetable; MIS built on unreconciled data misleads.
- Keep the pack to a few pages, with appendices for detail.
- Store prompts, scripts and templates centrally so any team member can produce the pack.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can AI produce an MIS report automatically?

It can pull data, build standard tables and charts, flag movements and draft commentary. The commentary and recommendations should be reviewed and rewritten by someone who knows the business before the pack goes to the client.

### What should a monthly MIS pack for a small business include?

Cash position and outlook, profitability against budget and prior year, the receivables and payables driving cash, and a short list of decisions needed. Supporting detail can go into appendices.

### What is the 45-day rule for MSME payments?

Under section 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006, the payment period agreed with a micro or small supplier cannot exceed 45 days from acceptance or deemed acceptance. Section 16 provides for compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate on delayed payments.

### Where should a CA practice start with AI in virtual CFO work?

Automate data collection and the standard tables first, then add anomaly flags and commentary drafts, keeping partner review on every pack.

# Income-tax Act, 2025 Transition: How a CA Firm Can Use AI to Remap Templates Safely

> How a CA firm can use AI to remap templates, checklists and client letters from the 1961 Act to the Income-tax Act, 2025 without trusting model-made section numbers.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-11-11-income-tax-act-2025-transition-how-a-ca-firm-can-use-ai-to-remap-templates-safely
Last updated: 2026-11-11

CA insights · 2026-11-11 · 6 min read

How a CA firm can use AI to remap templates, checklists and client letters from the 1961 Act to the Income-tax Act, 2025 without trusting model-made section numbers.

Key takeaways

- The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026; the Income-tax Rules, 2026 were notified on 20 March 2026 with new forms.
- Sections fell from 819 to 536 and chapters from 47 to 23; “tax year” replaces “previous year” and “assessment year”.
- Section 536 keeps the 1961 Act and its procedure for proceedings relating to tax years beginning before 1 April 2026, even if started later.
- Use the Income Tax Department’s comparison utilities as the source of truth; never let a model choose section numbers.
- Let AI extract references and redraft templates; keep the mapping, split provisions and which-Act decisions with named people.

Since 1 April 2026 every CA practice in India has been running two income-tax laws at once. Returns, notices and appeals for 2025-26 and earlier years still sit under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Income from 1 April 2026 falls under the Income-tax Act, 2025, with new section numbers, new rules and new forms. Meanwhile the firm’s engagement letters, checklists, notice-reply templates and client emails were mostly written for the old law.

Remapping all of that is exactly the kind of tedious, high-volume job firms want to hand to an AI tool. It is also the job where a general chatbot is most likely to be confidently wrong. This post sets out a method that uses AI for the volume and keeps the section numbers anchored to the official source.

## What actually changed, in four facts

- **Dates.** Parliament passed the Bill on 12 August 2025, it received the President’s assent on 21 August 2025, and it came into force on 1 April 2026, according to the [PIB release of 1 April 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2248005&lang=1&reg=3). The Income-tax Rules, 2026 were notified on 20 March 2026, with new forms.
- **Structure.** Sections fell from 819 to 536 and chapters from 47 to 23, with 39 new tables and 40 new formulas, as [reported by PTI at assent](https://www.thehindu.com/business/Economy/income-tax-act-gets-president-droupadi-murmus-assent/article69965067.ece).
- **Vocabulary.** “Previous year” and “assessment year” are replaced by a single “tax year”, the twelve months of the financial year starting 1 April (section 3 of the [Act as amended by the Finance Act, 2026](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/income_tax_act_2025_as_amended_by_fa_act_2026-pdf)).
- **Transition.** Section 536 repeals the 1961 Act but keeps it, and its procedure, for proceedings pending on 1 April 2026 and for proceedings started later, including notices, assessments, penalties and appeals, for any tax year beginning before 1 April 2026.

The [government’s own explainer](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/sep/doc202593626601.pdf) presents the Act as simplification, not a policy change. For a practice, that means most of the work is re-addressing: the same rule now sits at a different number, sometimes merged or split.

## Why a chatbot gets this wrong

General-purpose models learnt Indian tax law from six decades of material on the 1961 Act and comparatively little on the 2025 Act. Ask one for “the new section for 80C” and it may answer correctly (section 123), or it may produce a plausible number from a draft Bill, a blog post or nowhere. Both Acts also use the numbers 1 to 536, so a number can be valid in both and mean different things. A wrong reference in an engagement letter is embarrassing; a wrong reference in a reply to a notice is a problem.

The fix is not to avoid AI. It is to stop asking the model to remember section numbers, and make it look them up instead.

## The source of truth already exists

The Income Tax Department’s [Income-tax Act, 2025 page](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/income-tax-act-20251) has utilities that show a 1961 Act section next to its counterpart in the 2025 Act, and separate ones for Rules 1962 against Rules 2026 and for old forms against new forms. They can be used without logging in. Every mapping in your firm’s templates should trace back to one of these utilities or to the Act text itself, not to a model’s memory or a third-party table.

## A remapping workflow I would actually run

1. **Inventory.** List every document that cites the Act, Rules or forms: engagement letters, ITR and tax audit checklists, TDS rate charts, notice-reply templates, advance tax reminders, onboarding forms, standard client emails and any prompts your team already uses.
2. **Extract.** Use AI to pull every statutory reference into one table: document, paragraph, reference as written, and the sentence around it. This is pure extraction and models do it well. Spot-check a sample against the originals.
3. **Classify by tax year.** Mark each reference as relating to 2025-26 or earlier (stays on the 1961 Act under section 536), 2026-27 onwards (moves to the 2025 Act), or both.
4. **Map from the official utility.** A person, or a script reading a table built from the CBDT utility, fills in the new section, rule or form. The model does not choose numbers. Flag anything that maps to more than one provision, or to none, for a senior.
5. **Draft the new wording.** Now let AI rewrite the paragraph using the mapped reference. During the transition, dual references help clients and staff: “section 123 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 80C of the 1961 Act)”. Replace “assessment year” with “tax year” only where the document relates to 2026-27 onwards.
6. **Review and version.** A named reviewer approves each changed template, the old version is archived, and the mapping table is saved as the working paper.

Keep client data out of this exercise entirely: it is about templates, not files. Where a template carries client details, strip them first, in line with my [DPDP rubric for CA firms](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-19-dpdp-act-and-ai-in-ca-firms-in-india-a-client-data-decision-rubric).

Decision rubric for Income-tax Act, 2025 transition work. Evaluation framework only; adapt it to your practice. Not legal advice or benchmark data.

| Task | AI role | Minimum review gate | Stop if |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Extract references from templates | Automate | Sample check against originals | Scanned documents have not been OCR-checked |
| Old-to-new section mapping | Lookup only, from the CBDT utility | Every row cites the utility or Act text | A number came from the model’s memory |
| Split, merged or omitted provisions | Flag only | Senior reads both texts | The wording, not just the number, has changed |
| Rewriting template paragraphs | Draft | Reviewer approves each changed template | The draft introduces a reference not in the mapping table |
| Client explainer emails | Draft | Partner signs off the master version | It promises tax outcomes |
| Which Act governs a proceeding; grounds of appeal | Human only | Partner decision, recorded | Anyone relies on a tool’s summary of section 536 |

## Where judgement stays human

Three calls should not be delegated. First, which law governs a matter: a reassessment notice issued this year for 2023-24 runs under the 1961 Act and its procedure, by virtue of section 536, even though it is dated after 1 April 2026. Second, whether a provision has changed in substance and not just in number; the Finance Act, 2026 has already amended the new Act, so always read the current text. Third, anything in litigation, where existing grounds and citations stay on the old numbering. The [NIST AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) describes this as managing risk at the point of use: here, the tool prepares, a person decides, and the decision is written down.

The same thinking applies to the forms. My [tax audit post](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-09-ai-for-tax-audit-in-india-form-3cd-this-year-form-26-next-year) covers the move from Form 3CD to its successor, and the [TDS reconciliation guide](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-13-using-ai-for-tds-reconciliation-in-indian-ca-firms-from-26as-to-form-168) covers the statements side. To roll the remapping out across the firm, use the [90-day pilot structure](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-how-to-run-a-90-day-ai-pilot-in-a-ca-firm-in-india): one team, one set of templates, then scale.

## Monday-morning checklist

- Name one owner for the firm’s Act 2025 mapping table.
- Bookmark the CBDT utilities for sections, rules and forms, and ban model-generated section numbers in client documents.
- Inventory every template that cites the Act, Rules or forms.
- Tag each reference by tax year: 2025-26 and earlier, 2026-27 onwards, or both.
- Update engagement letters and advance tax reminders for 2026-27 first; they reach the most clients.
- Keep litigation files and pending-proceeding templates on 1961 Act references.

For the wider picture of AI in a practice, start from the [AI for Chartered Accountants in India hub](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-for-chartered-accountants-in-india). To see which compliance work is worth automating first, take the [free AI Opportunity Scorecard](https://pratikbajoria.com/scorecard), look at the scoped [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit), or [book a discovery call](https://pratikbajoria.com/#contact).

## Frequently asked questions

### Which income-tax law applies to FY 2025-26 income?

The Income-tax Act, 1961. Section 536 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 keeps the 1961 Act and its procedure for proceedings relating to any tax year beginning before 1 April 2026, including notices, assessments, penalties and appeals started after that date. Income from 1 April 2026 falls under the 2025 Act.

### Where can I check the new section number for an old section?

Use the utilities on the Income Tax Department’s Income-tax Act, 2025 page, which show a 1961 Act section beside its 2025 Act counterpart, with separate utilities for the Rules and the forms. Treat that, and the Act text, as the source of truth rather than a chatbot answer.

### Can AI update a CA firm’s templates for the Income-tax Act, 2025?

Yes, for extraction and drafting. AI can list every statutory reference in your templates and rewrite paragraphs once the mapping is fixed. The mapping itself should come from the official utility, and a named reviewer should approve each changed template.
