# AI and Articleship: How CA Firms Should Train Article Assistants Now

> Articleship is now two years, and AI drafts much of what articles used to learn on. A practical training plan for CA firms: review before preparation, manual fundamentals first, and clear tool rules.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-15-ai-and-articleship-how-ca-firms-should-train-article-assistants-now
Last updated: 2026-10-22

CA insights · 2026-10-15 · 7 min read

For most of us, articleship was where we learned the job by doing the repetitive parts: vouching, ticking, preparing schedules, chasing documents. A lot of that preparation can now be drafted by a tool in minutes. If firms keep training article assistants the old way, they will produce juniors who are good at work that is disappearing and untrained in the work that remains.

The time available has also shrunk. Under ICAI’s New Scheme of Education and Training, practical training is two years, so firms have less time to get it right. This is how I would redesign those two years, with the regulatory facts first and my practice view clearly marked as such.

## The training window under the new scheme

According to ICAI’s [FAQs on the New Scheme of Education and Training](https://resource.cdn.icai.org/75315bos-faqs-nset-july1.pdf), practical training starts after a student passes both groups of the Intermediate examination and completes the four-week ICITSS course, and lasts two years. Industrial training of 9 to 12 months is permitted in the last part of those two years, and 12 leaves are allowed in each year. The four-week Advanced ICITSS course comes after practical training and before the Final examination.

Two years, minus leave and exam preparation, is not much time to turn a student into someone a partner can rely on. That argues for being deliberate about what articles spend their hours on.

## The scheme in numbers

The figures below are all from ICAI’s own [FAQs](https://resource.cdn.icai.org/75315bos-faqs-nset-july1.pdf). They matter for planning because they fix how much of a student’s time is actually available to the firm.

Key timings under ICAI’s New Scheme of Education and Training. Source: ICAI Board of Studies FAQs.

| Item | What the scheme says | Why it matters to the firm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start of practical training | After passing both Intermediate groups and completing four-week ICITSS | Articles arrive with basic IT and soft-skills training already done |
| Duration | Two years | Plan the curriculum in quarters, not as an open-ended apprenticeship |
| Leave | 12 leaves in each year | Roughly 24 days across the term; schedule the manual fundamentals early |
| Industrial training | 9 to 12 months, in the last part of the two years | Some articles leave for industry before the busy season you planned around |
| Final exam eligibility | Practical training completed six months before the first day of the exam month | Expect exam leave and reduced availability late in the term |
| Advanced ICITSS | Four weeks, after practical training, before the Final | Not part of the firm’s two years |
| Self-paced online modules | Four sets (A to D); pass mark 50% per module | SET D includes Digital Ecosystem and Controls, a natural link to firm tool policies |

## The profession is already moving

ICAI has been unusually quick on AI. At its [AI Innovation Summit 2026](https://www.icai.org/post/icai-ais2026-26062026), the Institute said it had trained over 50,000 members in AI and developed more than 150 GPT-based tools, and it launched Level 3 of its AI certificate course for members. Students have their own tools too: ICAI’s [November 2024 release](https://icai.org/post/prc-icai-unveils-groundbreaking-ca-gpt-platform) reported a GPT for CA students covering Foundation, Intermediate and Final, with over 50,000 students using it at the time.

So articles will arrive already using AI. The firm’s job is not to introduce the tools; it is to teach professional habits around them.

## Teach review before preparation

The most valuable skill a junior can build now is checking machine output against evidence. I would restructure the first months of articleship around that.

- Give articles AI-drafted schedules with deliberate errors planted, and assess how many they find and how they prove each one.
- Make “show me the source document” the default response to any number an article presents, whoever or whatever produced it.
- Have articles write the review note on an AI draft, not just correct it, so the reasoning is visible.
- Rotate them through exception handling: the items a reconciliation tool could not match are where judgement is learned.

## Keep the fundamentals manual for a while

There is a real risk of juniors who can operate a tool but cannot do the underlying work. I would keep a short period of fully manual work on core tasks, such as a bank reconciliation, a GST return working and a set of audit vouching, before introducing AI on the same task. You cannot review what you have never done.

The internal audit standards make a similar point for the whole team. ICAI’s [SIA 240 on use of tools](https://internalaudit.icai.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Comp-of-Stnd-on-Internal-Audit-26.pdf) requires that the team has the competencies to use selected tools and that the engagement lead ensures periodic training as tools evolve. The same principle applies in any practice.

## A two-year plan, quarter by quarter

This is the structure I would use. It is a practice suggestion, not an ICAI requirement, and it assumes a mixed audit and tax practice.

- Quarter 1: manual fundamentals. Bank reconciliation, vouching, a GST return working and a TDS working done by hand, reviewed line by line.
- Quarter 2: review of machine output. The same tasks, now with AI-drafted versions containing planted errors; the article writes the review note.
- Quarters 3 and 4: evidence-heavy audit work, such as the clause-by-clause evidence index for CARO and the tax audit report, where tools prepare and articles check.
- Quarters 5 and 6: exception handling and client conversations. Unmatched items, notice replies and queries to management, with a senior present.
- Quarters 7 and 8: mentoring juniors and, for those leaving for industrial training, a handover file that shows their review notes.

## What to teach on real engagements

Two engagement types work especially well for this. In statutory audit, CARO reporting is mostly evidence assembly followed by a judgement, which makes it ideal for teaching the line between the two; I walk through it clause by clause in [AI for CARO 2020 reporting](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-16-ai-for-caro-2020-reporting-where-it-helps-and-where-judgement-stays). For working papers generally, [AI for audit working papers in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-30-ai-for-audit-working-papers-in-india-what-a-ca-should-automate-and-what-must-stay-human) covers what SA 230 still demands of the file whoever drafted it.

On the tax side, [AI for tax audit in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-09-ai-for-tax-audit-in-india-form-3cd-this-year-form-26-next-year) is a good second-year assignment: lots of data matching, and a clear point where a CA has to sign. If articles move faster because of tools, the firm also has to think about how that shows up in fees, which I discuss in [how CA firms should price work when AI cuts the hours](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-14-how-ca-firms-in-india-should-price-work-when-ai-cuts-the-hours).

## Rules articles should know on day one

None of this needs a large programme. A one-page policy, a planted-error exercise in the first month, and partners who ask “how do you know?” consistently will do more than any course. If you are weighing formal courses for the team, I compared the options in [AI courses for chartered accountants in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-ai-courses-for-chartered-accountants-in-india-what-is-worth-it). For the firm-wide plan, start from the [AI for Chartered Accountants in India hub](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-for-chartered-accountants-in-india).

- Which AI tools are approved, and that client data never goes into personal accounts.
- What may be drafted by AI, and what must be done or concluded by a person.
- That every AI-assisted output is labelled as such in the file until reviewed.
- Who to ask when an AI answer and their own work disagree, and that disagreement is worth raising.

## How to tell whether it is working

Measure the habit, not the tool. At the end of each quarter I would look at three things for every article: the share of planted errors they found, whether their review notes cite a source document for each point, and how many exceptions they escalated rather than cleared on their own. If those numbers improve, the training is working, whatever tools they used along the way.

A firm that wants to try this formally can treat the first cohort as a pilot, with a baseline and a go or stop decision at the end, using the approach in [how to run a 90-day AI pilot in a CA firm](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-how-to-run-a-90-day-ai-pilot-in-a-ca-firm-in-india).

## Frequently asked questions

### How long is CA articleship now?

Under ICAI’s New Scheme of Education and Training, practical training is two years, started after passing both groups of the Intermediate examination and completing ICITSS. Industrial training of 9 to 12 months is permitted in the last part.

### How many leaves are allowed during articleship?

ICAI’s FAQs on the new scheme allow 12 leaves in each year of the two-year practical training.

### Should article assistants use AI?

Yes, within firm rules on approved tools and client data, and after they have done the core tasks manually at least once. The priority is teaching them to review AI output against evidence.

### What AI training does ICAI offer?

ICAI runs an AI certificate course for members, with Level 3 launched at its AI Innovation Summit 2026, and provides CA GPT tools for members and students. It reported training over 50,000 members in AI by June 2026.

### What skills matter most for juniors now?

Checking outputs against source documents, writing clear review notes, handling exceptions and knowing when to escalate. Preparation still matters, but review is where trust is built.

### When can a student sit the CA Final under the new scheme?

According to ICAI’s FAQs, after registering for the Final, completing practical training six months before the first day of the exam month, completing Advanced ICITSS and qualifying all four self-paced online modules.

# How CA Firms in India Should Price Work When AI Cuts the Hours

> If AI halves preparation time, hourly billing hands the gain to the client. How Indian CA firms can price scope and risk instead, within ICAI’s rules on fees.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-14-how-ca-firms-in-india-should-price-work-when-ai-cuts-the-hours
Last updated: 2026-10-22

CA insights · 2026-10-14 · 4 min read

Every partner I speak to about AI eventually asks the same uncomfortable question: if this saves my team hours, and I bill by the hour or by a rate card built on hours, have I just cut my own fees?

Possibly. But only if pricing stays where it is. The more useful question is what the client is actually paying for, and whether that has changed. In most compliance and advisory work it has not: they are paying for a correct deliverable, delivered on time, with a professional standing behind it.

## How much time are we talking about?

Nobody has a reliable India-specific number for CA practices yet, and I would be wary of anyone who quotes one. The broader surveys give a sense of direction. Thomson Reuters’ [2025 Future of Professionals report](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/the-ai-adoption-reality-check-firms-with-ai-strategies-are-twice-as-likely-to-see-ai-driven-revenue-growth-those-without-risk-falling-behind-302490973.html), based on 2,275 professionals across legal, tax, accounting, audit, risk and trade, found respondents expecting AI to save five hours a week within a year. The same report found only 22% saying their organisation had a visible, defined AI strategy.

In India, Microsoft’s [2025 Work Trend Index findings](https://news.microsoft.com/source/asia/2025/08/20/indias-workforce-goes-ai-first-as-frontier-firms-lead-the-transformation-microsoft-work-trend-index-2025/) reported that 93% of leaders intend to use AI agents to extend workforce capacity in the next 12 to 18 months. Clients will read the same headlines. Expect them to ask why the fee has not moved.

## First, know what you are not allowed to do

The obvious answer, "charge for the outcome", runs into the profession’s own rules. Under Clause (10) of Part I of the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, read with [Regulation 192](https://icai.org/post/5645), a CA in practice may not charge fees based on a percentage of profits or contingent upon the findings or results of the work, apart from specific exceptions such as receivers and liquidators, co-operative society audits and valuers for direct taxes. ICAI’s FAQs also say fees cannot be charged as a percentage of turnover except as Regulation 192 allows.

So for audit, tax and most compliance work, "value pricing" in an Indian practice means pricing the scope, the complexity and the risk of the engagement as a fixed fee agreed upfront, not tying the fee to a result.

## Price the deliverable, not the hours behind it

A fixed fee per deliverable lets the firm keep the efficiency it earns. The client gets certainty and a defined scope; the firm gets the benefit of doing the work faster. That only works if the scope is written down clearly, which is why I would revisit engagement letters at the same time. [SA 210’s illustrative engagement letters](https://www.icai.org/post/aasb-illustrative-audit-engagement-letter-under-companies-act-2013-17-12-2014) already provide for fees and billing arrangements to be agreed in writing; extend the same discipline to non-audit work.

- Define the deliverable: which returns, which reconciliations, which reports, by when.
- Define what is out of scope and how it will be priced, such as notices, revisions and additional entities.
- State what the client must provide and by when; late or messy data is the biggest driver of hours.
- Separate the review and sign-off component, which does not shrink with AI, from preparation, which does.

## What does not get cheaper

Review time, professional judgement and liability do not fall with AI. If anything, review becomes more important, because more of the first draft is produced by a tool. I would make that visible in proposals: a smaller preparation line, an unchanged review and sign-off line, and new lines for work that AI makes possible, such as monthly exception reports or faster turnaround on queries.

## Where the time saved should go

If the hours saved simply disappear into lower bills, the firm has funded the tools and given away the benefit. Decide before you roll AI out where the time will be redeployed, and measure it during a [time-boxed pilot](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-how-to-run-a-90-day-ai-pilot-in-a-ca-firm-in-india) rather than guessing.

- Into review quality: more time for the manager and partner on the judgement areas.
- Into new recurring services clients will pay for, such as monthly MIS or compliance health checks.
- Into capacity, so the firm can take on more clients in peak season without lowering standards.
- Into training, so article assistants and juniors learn to review machine output, not just prepare.

Faster preparation changes how juniors learn as well as what clients pay; I cover that in [AI and articleship](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-15-ai-and-articleship-how-ca-firms-should-train-article-assistants-now). For an example of work where the evidence is cheaper to assemble but the judgement is not, see [AI for CARO 2020 reporting](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-16-ai-for-caro-2020-reporting-where-it-helps-and-where-judgement-stays) and [AI for audit working papers in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-30-ai-for-audit-working-papers-in-india-what-a-ca-should-automate-and-what-must-stay-human).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a CA firm charge fees based on results?

Generally no. Clause (10) of Part I of the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act and Regulation 192 prohibit fees based on a percentage of profits or contingent on findings or results, subject to specific exceptions such as receivers, liquidators, co-operative society audits and valuers for direct taxes.

### Should a CA firm reduce fees because it uses AI?

Not automatically. Clients pay for a correct, timely deliverable with professional responsibility behind it. A fixed fee for a clearly defined scope lets the firm keep efficiency gains while giving the client certainty.

### How much time does AI save accountants?

There is no reliable India-specific figure yet. In Thomson Reuters’ 2025 Future of Professionals survey of 2,275 professionals, respondents expected AI to save five hours a week within the next year.

### What should change in proposals?

Separate preparation from review and sign-off, define scope and exclusions precisely, and price new AI-enabled services, such as monthly exception reporting, as their own line.

# Using AI for TDS Reconciliation in Indian CA Firms: From 26AS to Form 168

> Form 26AS is now Form 168 under the new Act. How to automate TDS matching and the mismatch list, while a reviewer decides what to chase with the deductor.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-13-using-ai-for-tds-reconciliation-in-indian-ca-firms-from-26as-to-form-168
Last updated: 2026-10-22

CA insights · 2026-10-13 · 4 min read

TDS reconciliation is one of the least glamorous and most useful places to put AI in a practice. The volume is high, the rules are clear, and the cost of a missed mismatch is a demand, a refund delay or an uncomfortable call with the client.

It is also changing names. Under the [Income-tax Act, 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2248005), the statement many of us still call 26AS is [Form No. 168, the Annual Information Statement](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-168-faqs), issued under section 510 read with Rule 245. The work behind it has not changed: match what the client booked with what others reported, and chase the differences.

## What the statement now contains

The Department’s [Form 168 FAQs](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-168-faqs) describe two parts. Part A carries general information about the taxpayer. Part B carries TDS and TCS information, Statement of Financial Transactions data from reporting entities, payment of taxes, demands and refunds, and other information such as dividends, interest on refunds, and securities and mutual fund transactions. The Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS) aggregates this by category and is updated after feedback is processed.

In practice a reconciliation now has two jobs: tie the TDS credits the client is claiming to what deductors reported, and make sure the income behind those credits is fully reflected in the books and the return.

## What to automate

None of this needs a clever model. A well-written script does most of it, and an AI assistant is useful for writing and maintaining that script, for reading messy ledger narrations and for drafting the deductor emails. Gartner’s [2025 AI in Finance survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-18-gartner-survey-shows-finance-ai-adoption-remains-steady-in-2025) found error and anomaly detection among the three most common finance AI use cases; TDS matching is a very practical version of it.

- Parsing the downloaded statement into a clean table by deductor TAN, section, date and amount.
- Matching each entry to the client’s ledger, first exactly, then within tolerances on date and amount, with every fuzzy match labelled as such.
- Producing a mismatch list in three buckets: in the statement but not in the books, in the books but not in the statement, and in both with different amounts.
- Drafting the email to each deductor listing the missing or short-reported entries, with invoice references attached.
- Tracking responses and re-running the match after deductors file corrections.

## What a reviewer still decides

Whether a difference is a timing issue, a deductor error, a booking error or income the client has not recognised is a judgement. So is the decision to submit feedback on an AIS entry, to wait for a correction statement, or to report income that does not appear in the statement at all. The [FAQs](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-168-faqs) are explicit that actual income must be reported even if it is missing from the AIS, and that the TIS cannot be edited directly.

I would also keep a person on any match the tool marks as fuzzy. Fuzzy matching is where reconciliations quietly go wrong: two invoices of similar value from the same customer can be paired incorrectly, and the error will not surface until a deductor’s correction breaks it.

## The tax auditor will ask the deductor-side question too

For clients who deduct tax, the new tax audit report raises the bar. [Form 26](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs) asks the auditor for the total number of transactions reported and not reported in the TDS/TCS return as it stands after the latest correction statement, and the amount of transactions not reported. A firm that already runs transaction-level matching for its clients’ own credits can extend the same scripts to their deduction compliance.

## A simple monthly rhythm

If this is the firm’s first AI workflow, run it as a time-boxed pilot with a baseline, as in my [90-day pilot playbook](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-how-to-run-a-90-day-ai-pilot-in-a-ca-firm-in-india).

- Download the statement and the ledger extract on a fixed day each month or quarter.
- Run the match and publish the three-bucket mismatch list to the reviewer.
- Reviewer classifies each item and approves the deductor emails.
- Re-run after corrections, and close items with a note of how they were resolved.
- Before the return, reconcile income heads in the TIS to the books and document every difference.

TDS matching is also a good early exercise for article assistants; see [AI and articleship](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-15-ai-and-articleship-how-ca-firms-should-train-article-assistants-now). For the statutory dues clause in the companies audit report, see [AI for CARO 2020 reporting](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-16-ai-for-caro-2020-reporting-where-it-helps-and-where-judgement-stays).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Form 26AS still available?

Under the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026, the Annual Information Statement is Form No. 168, corresponding to Form 26AS and section 285BB under the 1961 Act.

### Can AI reconcile TDS automatically?

It can do the parsing, matching and drafting at high volume. A reviewer should still classify each difference, approve deductor follow-ups and decide on AIS feedback, and any fuzzy match should be confirmed by a person.

### What if income is missing from the AIS?

According to the Department’s FAQs, all actual income must be reported in the return even if it does not appear in the AIS.

### What does Form 26 ask about TDS returns?

For assessees who deduct or collect tax, the auditor reports the number of transactions reported and not reported in the TDS/TCS return after the latest correction, and the amount of transactions not reported.

## Sources

- [Income Tax Department: Form No. 168 (Annual Information Statement) FAQs](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-168-faqs)
- [Income Tax Department: Form No. 26 FAQs (tax audit under section 63, Income-tax Act, 2025)](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs)
- [PIB: Income-tax Act, 2025 comes into force from 1 April 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2248005)

# Drafting Replies to GST and Income Tax Notices With AI Without Losing Control

> A GST or income-tax notice reply is a legal position with a deadline. Here is the clock for ASMT-10, section 74A and appeals, the e-proceedings rules, and where AI helps.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-12-drafting-replies-to-gst-and-income-tax-notices-with-ai-without-losing-control
Last updated: 2026-10-22

CA insights · 2026-10-12 · 8 min read

Two facts shape every notice reply I review. A GST scrutiny notice in Form ASMT-10 gives the taxpayer 30 days from service to explain, unless the officer allows longer. And a response submitted through the income-tax e-proceedings facility [cannot be edited once it is filed](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/respond-to-e-proceedings-faq). Put those together and the risk of AI in notice work is obvious: a fast, fluent draft that nobody checked becomes a permanent record before a tax officer.

That is not an argument for avoiding AI. A good reply is mostly organisation: the timeline, the documents, the reconciliation and the relevant provisions, and AI is very good at organisation. The legal position taken on a client’s behalf is a different matter. Below I set out the clock for the common notices, then split the work between the tool and the CA who signs off, using a GST scrutiny notice and an income-tax mismatch query as the two examples.

## Know the clock before you open a tool

Deadlines decide how much drafting help you can afford to verify. For GST return scrutiny, [Rule 99 of the CGST Rules](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter11/rule99_v1.00.html) has the proper officer issue Form GST ASMT-10 seeking an explanation within 30 days of service, or a longer period the officer allows. The taxpayer replies in ASMT-11, and if the explanation is accepted the officer issues ASMT-12.

For demands relating to financial year 2024-25 onwards, [section 74A of the CGST Act](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/acts/2017_CGST_act/active/chapter15/Section74A_v1.00.html) sets a single framework: the show cause notice must be issued within 42 months from the due date for the annual return of that year, and the order within 12 months of the notice, extendable by up to six months by a senior officer for recorded reasons.

On the income-tax side, remember that the [Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2248005). Check which Act and which section a notice cites before anyone, human or machine, starts drafting.

Key GST and income-tax notice timelines, from the official texts. Check the notice itself: an officer may allow a longer period, and dates run from service or communication.

| Stage | Form or channel | Time limit | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GST scrutiny of returns: explanation sought | ASMT-10, reply in ASMT-11 | 30 days from service of the notice, or a longer period the officer allows | [Rule 99, CGST Rules](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter11/rule99_v1.00.html) |
| GST demand, FY 2024-25 onwards: show cause notice | Section 74A | Within 42 months from the due date of the annual return for the year | [Section 74A, CGST Act](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/acts/2017_CGST_act/active/chapter15/Section74A_v1.00.html) |
| GST demand, FY 2024-25 onwards: order | Section 74A | Within 12 months of the notice, extendable by up to six months for recorded reasons | [Section 74A, CGST Act](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/acts/2017_CGST_act/active/chapter15/Section74A_v1.00.html) |
| GST appeal against an order | Appeal to the Appellate Authority | Three months from communication of the order; a further one month may be allowed for sufficient cause | [Section 107, CGST Act](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/acts/2017_CGST_act/active/chapter18/section107_v1.00.html) |
| GST appeal: pre-deposit | With the appeal | The admitted amount in full, plus 10% of the tax in dispute, capped at ₹20 crore under the CGST Act | [Section 107(6), CGST Act](https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/acts/2017_CGST_act/active/chapter18/section107_v1.00.html) |
| Income-tax notices and intimations | e-Proceedings on the e-filing portal | As stated in the notice; the submit button can lapse after the response due date for CPC notices | [e-Proceedings FAQ](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/respond-to-e-proceedings-faq) |

The appeal clock matters for drafting because the reply at notice stage is the record the appellate authority will read later. A weak or inconsistent reply drafted in a hurry is hard to repair three months on.

## What AI does well in notice work

- Reading a long notice and listing every specific discrepancy or allegation, with the paragraph it appears in, so nothing is missed in the reply.
- Building a dated chronology from the client’s returns, correspondence and payment records.
- Producing the reconciliation the officer is implicitly asking for, for example GSTR-1 against GSTR-3B, or books against the figures in the [Annual Information Statement](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-168-faqs).
- Drafting a first version of the reply in a clear structure: facts, reconciliation, submissions, documents enclosed.
- Preparing the index of annexures and checking that every document referred to is actually attached.

## What stays with a named CA

Three things. First, the facts check: every number in the reply ties to a source document the reviewer has seen. Second, the legal position: whether to accept and pay, contest, or partly accept, and on what grounds. Third, the decision to file and the filing itself.

I would add a fourth for AI drafts specifically: every provision, circular or case cited must be checked against the official text. General-purpose assistants still produce confident references that do not exist or do not say what the draft claims. A reply that cites a non-existent judgment does more damage than a short reply that cites none.

## Mismatch queries start in the AIS

Many income-tax queries begin with a difference between the return and what third parties reported. The Department’s [Form 168 FAQs](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-168-faqs) explain that the Annual Information Statement shows transactions reported by banks, employers, fund houses, brokers and registrars, and that inaccurate entries should be corrected through the feedback option on the portal. The same FAQs make the point that all actual income must be reported even if it is missing from the AIS.

This is a good place for AI-assisted preparation before any notice arrives: compare the AIS with the client’s books each year, list differences, and draft the feedback or explanation while the facts are fresh.

## Income-tax e-proceedings: what the portal allows

The Department’s [e-Proceedings user manual](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/respond-to-e-proceedings) says the service lets any registered user view and respond to notices, intimations and letters from the Assessing Officer, CPC or any other income-tax authority, including defective-return notices, prima facie adjustments and suo motu rectifications. A taxpayer can add an authorised representative to respond on their behalf, and each submission generates a transaction ID.

Three portal rules change how I use AI here. Responses can be marked as full or partial, so a holding partial response with the key reconciliation is often better than a rushed full one. Submitted responses can be viewed but [not edited](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/respond-to-e-proceedings-faq). And for CPC notices the submit button becomes inactive once the response due date has lapsed. Build the AI-assisted draft early, but treat the upload as a one-way door that a named CA opens.

## A review checklist before anything is filed

I use this list on every AI-assisted reply. It is short on purpose, so that people actually use it under deadline pressure.

- The notice section, Act and tax period are confirmed against the notice itself, including whether it cites the Income-tax Act, 1961 or the Income-tax Act, 2025.
- The deadline is diaried from the date of service or communication, not the date the client forwarded the notice.
- Every figure in the draft ties to a return, the books or the AIS, with the working on file.
- Every section, rule, circular and case cited has been opened and read in the official text.
- The legal position (accept, contest or partly accept) is recorded as the reviewing CA’s decision.
- Annexures listed in the reply match the files actually uploaded.
- The AI draft, the reviewer’s changes and the filed version are all kept on the client file.

## Client data rules for notice work

Notice files contain more personal and sensitive data than almost any other work in a practice. Use firm-controlled tools with retention settings you have checked, and share only what the task needs. The [DPDP Rules, 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2190014) were notified in November 2025 with an 18-month phased timeline, which is enough time to set this up properly but not enough to ignore it. My [AI controls checklist for CA firms](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-controls-checklist-ca-firms-india) covers the wider review gates.

- No client notice goes into a personal chatbot account.
- Redact identifiers where the task does not need them.
- Keep the AI draft, the reviewer’s changes and the final filed reply in the file.
- Log who reviewed and approved each reply.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long do I have to reply to a GST ASMT-10 notice?

Rule 99 of the CGST Rules provides for an explanation within 30 days of service of the notice, or such further period as the proper officer may permit. The reply is filed in Form GST ASMT-11.

### Can I use ChatGPT to draft a reply to a tax notice?

You can use an approved, firm-controlled assistant to organise facts and prepare a first draft. A CA must check every fact and citation against source documents and official texts, decide the legal position, and approve the final reply before filing.

### What is the time limit under section 74A of the CGST Act?

For financial year 2024-25 onwards, the show cause notice must be issued within 42 months from the due date for furnishing the annual return for that year, and the order within 12 months of the notice, extendable by up to six months.

### How do I correct a wrong entry in the AIS?

Open the AIS on the e-filing portal, select the transaction and submit feedback with the appropriate reason, such as incorrect, duplicate or not related. The Taxpayer Information Summary updates after the feedback is processed; it cannot be edited directly.

### Can I edit a response after submitting it on the income-tax e-filing portal?

No. The Income Tax Department’s e-Proceedings FAQ says a response cannot be edited once submitted. You can view what was submitted, so check the draft fully before uploading.

### How long do I have to file a GST appeal against an order?

Section 107 of the CGST Act allows three months from the date the order is communicated, and the Appellate Authority may allow a further one month if there was sufficient cause for the delay. A pre-deposit of the admitted amount plus 10% of the disputed tax is required.

# Finance AI ROI for Mid-Market Companies in India: A CA's Decision Rubric

> How to measure AI ROI for finance teams in India: a CA’s decision rubric for mid-market CFOs covering baseline, cost, payback, controls and a Monday checklist.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-12-finance-ai-roi-for-mid-market-companies-in-india-a-cas-decision-rubric
Last updated: 2026-10-12

CA insights · 2026-10-12 · 7 min read

How to measure AI ROI for finance teams in India: a CA’s decision rubric for mid-market CFOs covering baseline, cost, payback, controls and a Monday checklist.

Key takeaways

- ROI for finance AI is a measurement design problem before it is a model problem: baseline one workflow, then compare the same metrics after a fixed period.
- Put review time, exception handling and training on the cost side; omitting them invents a false payback.
- Score each candidate use case on value, feasibility, control risk and measurement clarity before you fund licences.
- A project without a named metric owner, a human gate or a stop condition is not ready to claim return.
- Indian mid-market teams should treat DPDP safeguards and professional confidentiality as part of the cost of a defensible deployment, not as optional extras.

When a mid-market CFO in India asks me whether finance AI will pay for itself, they are rarely looking for a vendor’s “three-to-one” slide. They want a decision they can defend to the board, the auditor and their own team: which workflow, which number, which cost, and when we stop if it does not move. I write as Pratik Bajoria, Chartered Accountant, ex-Big 4, and founder of Findost. This piece is a measurement rubric, not a catalogue of tools and not a promise of outcomes.

I have written elsewhere about why the finance function is often a sensible first place to deploy AI, how to prove payback before you buy, and how CFOs can sequence automation over ninety days. What those conversations still lack, in many companies, is a shared definition of return. Without that definition, every pilot “succeeds” in the room that funded it and fails on the P&L.

## What “ROI” should mean for a finance team

In a mid-market finance function, return is almost never a single rupee figure on day one. It is usually a combination of hours released from repetitive work, shorter cycle time on close or reconciliations, fewer rework loops, and sometimes earlier cash visibility. The right definition is the one your leadership already manages: days to close, items aged in reconciliations, invoice cycle time, exception rate, or hours of senior review per pack. Inventing a new vanity metric for AI is how programmes hide.

Two rules keep the conversation honest. First, measure one workflow at a time. Bundling “AI for finance” into one score makes it impossible to know what worked. Second, take the baseline before any tool runs. Rough logs of volume, hours by role and known error patterns for two or three weeks beat a confident estimate after the fact. If you cannot baseline it, you cannot claim ROI for it.

## Put the full cost on the same sheet

The most common error I see is counting only the licence. A defensible cost side includes software and usage fees, any integration or data cleanup, the hours reviewers spend checking output, training and change management, and the cost of exceptions the tool creates. Review time belongs on the cost side even when the tool is “free” inside an existing suite, because senior minutes are the scarce resource in most Indian mid-market finance teams.

There is also a control cost that rarely appears on vendor ROI sheets. Where personal data sits in payroll, vendor masters or customer records, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 expects reasonable security safeguards, including when a processor handles that data on your behalf. Professional confidentiality obligations under ICAI’s framework do not pause because a model is convenient. Treat approved environments, retention settings and logging as part of the cost of a deployment you can stand behind — not as optional polish after the pilot “works”.

Public risk frameworks help structure that conversation without turning it into theatre. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organises the work as govern, map, measure and manage; its generative AI profile is a useful prompt list for documentation and human oversight. Use them as checklists against your own chart of accounts and staffing, not as a substitute for either.

## A decision rubric you can score in one meeting

Before you fund a licence or a build, score each candidate use case against the axes below. I use a one-to-five scale. Anything that cannot clear a basic threshold on measurement clarity or control risk does not get an ROI conversation yet — it gets a redesign.

Evaluation framework only. Score your own use cases; this is not benchmark or market-share data.

| Axis | What good looks like (5) | Red flag (1) | Your score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Value clarity | Tied to a metric leadership already reviews (close days, exceptions, cycle time, cash timing) | “Productivity” or “innovation” with no named number | \_\_\_ |
| Baseline | Two to three weeks of volume, hours by role and error/rework logged before the tool runs | Baseline promised after go-live | \_\_\_ |
| Full cost | Licences, integration, review time, training and exception handling on one sheet | Licence price alone treated as total cost | \_\_\_ |
| Feasibility | Data extractable, process stable, owner named | Needs clean data you do not have, or nobody owns the metric | \_\_\_ |
| Control risk | Human gate before anything reaches books, filings or external parties; approved environment | Unreviewed output can hit the ledger, a client or a regulator | \_\_\_ |
| Measurement window | Fixed review date and stop conditions written before start | Open-ended “pilot” with no decision date | \_\_\_ |
| Attribution | You can say what changed because of the tool versus other process fixes | Every improvement credited to AI by default | \_\_\_ |

Notice that model quality barely appears. For mid-market finance AI ROI in India, the deciding factors are usually measurement design and control design. A weaker model with a clean baseline and a named reviewer will beat a stronger model with neither.

## How I would run the first payback test

Pick one workflow with volume and clear rules — bank categorisation, invoice intake, reconciliation exception lists, or a recurring MIS first draft are typical starting points. Write the five-line map: input, decision, output, owner, definition of good. Log the baseline. Agree the human gate and the data classes the tool may see. Run the assisted version beside the old process for a fixed window, with an exception log reviewed weekly. At the decision date, compare the same metrics and write go, adjust or stop. Stopping with evidence is a legitimate ROI outcome: it frees budget for the next candidate.

If the team cannot explain the workflow and the metric in five minutes on a Monday, the measurement design is not ready. That operating habit is the same one I describe in [the Monday morning test for any AI workflow](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-29-the-monday-morning-test-for-any-ai-workflow). For sequencing across close, payables and reporting, use the [finance automation roadmap for CFOs and controllers](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-04-ai-finance-automation-roadmap-for-cfos-and-controllers) rather than trying to claim ROI on five workflows at once.

## What I would not count as ROI

I would not count a polished demo, a reduction in “clicks”, or an associate’s enthusiasm as return. I would not annualise two quiet weeks into a full-year saving without a busy-period test. I would not credit AI for improvements that came from cleaning the data or rewriting the SOP unless you can separate those effects. And I would not let a securities-market disclosure narrative substitute for operational evidence: if you are listed or listing-adjacent, treat SEBI’s public materials as part of your compliance reading list, but do not confuse regulatory language with measured payback on a finance workflow.

For the wider CA and finance implementation map, start at the [AI for chartered accountants in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-for-chartered-accountants-in-india) hub. On proving payback before purchase, see [how do you know finance AI will pay for itself before you buy](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-21-how-do-you-know-finance-ai-will-pay-for-itself-before-you-buy); on why finance is often the right starting point, see [the finance function as AI’s highest-ROI starting point](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-17-the-finance-function-is-ai-s-highest-roi-starting-point); for assistant choice once the metric is clear, see [ChatGPT, Copilot or Gemini for a CA firm](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-05-chatgpt-vs-copilot-vs-gemini-how-a-ca-firm-in-india-should-choose-an-ai-assistant). To score your own opportunities, take the free [AI Opportunity Scorecard](https://pratikbajoria.com/scorecard), look at the scoped [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit), or [book a discovery call](https://pratikbajoria.com/#contact).

## Monday-morning checklist

- Name one finance workflow and the metric leadership already reviews.
- Log two to three weeks of baseline volume, hours by role and rework before any tool runs.
- Put licences, integration, review time, training and exception handling on one cost sheet.
- Score the use case on the rubric above; redesign anything weak on control risk or measurement clarity.
- Write the human gate, approved environment and stop conditions on one page.
- Fix a decision date; compare the same metrics, then go, adjust or stop in writing.
- Refuse to claim ROI from demos, quiet weeks alone, or improvements you cannot attribute.

## Frequently asked questions

### How should a mid-market finance team in India measure AI ROI?

Baseline one workflow before any tool runs: volume, hours by role, cycle time and error or rework rate. Add the full cost of change — licences, integration, review time and training — then compare the same metrics after a fixed period. ROI is only meaningful when the numerator and denominator are both measured on your own books, not on a vendor slide.

### What costs should be included in finance AI ROI?

Include software and usage fees, any integration or data work, the hours reviewers spend checking output, training and change management, and the cost of exceptions the tool creates. Leaving review time out of the cost side is the most common way mid-market teams invent a false payback.

### When is a finance AI project not ready to claim ROI?

When there is no written baseline, no named owner for the metric, no human review gate, or when the only evidence is a demo. If you cannot explain the workflow and the number in five minutes on a Monday, you are not measuring return — you are narrating hope.

# AI for Tax Audit in India: Form 3CD This Year, Form 26 Next Year

> Form 26 replaces Form 3CD from tax year 2026-27. Where AI helps a CA prepare tax audit data, and where the reported position must stay with the signer.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-09-ai-for-tax-audit-in-india-form-3cd-this-year-form-26-next-year
Last updated: 2026-10-22

CA insights · 2026-10-09 · 5 min read

**Key takeaways**

- Form No. 26 under section 63 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 applies for tax years beginning on or after 1 April 2026; Forms 3CA, 3CB and 3CD continue for assessment years up to 2026-27.
- AI helps with the data work: ledger scrutiny, TDS/TCS reconciliation, cross-checking books against the Annual Information Statement and drafting document requests.
- Clause answers, the classification of observations and the signature stay with the accountant.
- Form 26 asks for the IP address and country of the server holding electronic books and the address of the India-located daily backup (Rule 46).
- Use the remaining Form 3CD season as a pilot before Form 26 work starts.

Tax audit is about to change shape, and that makes this a sensible moment to decide where AI belongs in it. The [Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2248005), and with it a new tax audit report: [Form No. 26 under section 63](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs), which applies to tax years beginning on or after 1 April 2026. For audits relating to assessment year 2026-27 and earlier, Forms 3CA, 3CB and 3CD [continue to apply](https://taxguru.in/income-tax/ay-2026-27-tax-audit-forms-3ca-3cb-3cd-apply-form-26-starts.html).

So most practices will run one more season on Form 3CD while preparing for a form that is built very differently. In both, my view is the same: AI can do a great deal of the data work behind the clauses, and none of the reporting judgement.

## What actually changes with Form 26

The Department’s [Form 26 FAQs](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs) describe a report in four parts: Part A for the assessee’s particulars, Part B for the statement of particulars under section 63, Part C where accounts are audited under another law (the old Form 3CA case) and Part D where they are not (the old Form 3CB case). The signing accountant must quote a UDIN, and the firm registration number where the audit is in the firm’s name.

- Business threshold: total sales, turnover or gross receipts above ₹1 crore, rising to ₹10 crore where cash receipts and cash payments each stay within 5% of the total ([Form 26 FAQ 3](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs)).
- Profession threshold: gross receipts above ₹50 lakh.
- Due date: one month before the return due date, so 30 September or 31 October depending on the return deadline.

Three design choices matter for automation. Every clause in Part B needs a mandatory Yes or No answer. Detailed schedules are triggered only when a clause is answered Yes. And the FAQs say the data has been aligned with the return of income so that it can, going forward, be used to populate the ITR. That is a structured-data report, which is exactly the kind of work machines handle well, and exactly the kind where one wrong flag flows straight into the return.

## Where AI genuinely helps in tax audit preparation

Most of the hours in a tax audit go into pulling, classifying and tying out data rather than forming opinions. That is where I would point AI first, always on data the firm controls.

- Ledger scrutiny for clause-relevant items: payments that could breach cash limits, expenses that may be personal or capital in nature, and entries that need a second look before the clause answer is drafted.
- Reconciling TDS and TCS. Form 26 asks the auditor for the number of transactions reported and not reported in the TDS/TCS returns as they stand after the latest correction, and the amount not reported ([FAQ 38](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs)). Matching ledgers to returns at transaction level is tedious and well suited to scripts.
- Cross-checking the client’s books against the [Annual Information Statement](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-168-faqs), so that differences are explained before the report is signed rather than after a notice arrives.
- Drafting the first version of the explanatory notes and the list of documents to request from the client.

## Where it must not decide

Form 26 asks the auditor to classify every observation or qualification clause-wise as made on a test-check basis applying materiality, based on management representation, or as something the auditor was unable to verify ([FAQ 35](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs)). It also asks for the impact on profit, loss or book profit of qualifications and other matters in the statutory audit ([FAQ 36](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs)). Those are judgements about evidence. An AI tool can help assemble the evidence; it cannot decide which category applies, and it cannot sign.

The same goes for every Yes or No answer that carries a tax consequence. I would let AI propose an answer with the supporting ledger extract, and require the engagement partner or manager to accept each one explicitly. If the reviewer cannot see why the tool proposed Yes, the answer stays blank until they can.

## Watch the new data-location question

One Form 26 change touches technology directly. Under Rule 46, where books of account are kept electronically they must remain accessible in India at all times, with a daily backup on servers located in India, and Form 26 asks for the IP address and country of the server holding the accounting data and the address of the India-located backup server ([FAQ 18](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/documents/d/guest/form-26-faqs)).

That has two consequences for a practice. You will need to ask clients where their cloud accounting data actually sits, and you should ask the same question of any AI or data tool your own team uses on client books. If a tool cannot tell you where it stores and processes data, it is not ready for tax audit work.

## How I would prepare a practice this year

Use the remaining Form 3CD season as the pilot. Pick two or three clause areas with heavy data work, script the extraction and matching, and keep the reviewer’s sign-off on every output. By the time Form 26 work starts for tax year 2026-27, the firm will know which steps are reliable and which still need a human doing them end to end. My [90-day pilot playbook](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-how-to-run-a-90-day-ai-pilot-in-a-ca-firm-in-india) sets out how to run that test.

- Map each Form 26 Part B clause to the data source in the client’s books.
- Build reusable checks for the high-volume clauses first: TDS/TCS, loans and deposits by mode, and quantitative details for trading and manufacturing clients.
- Write down, per clause, what the tool may propose and what only a reviewer may conclude.
- Ask every client about server location and backups before fieldwork, not during it.

The same evidence often feeds the companies audit report. For the CARO side, see [AI for CARO 2020 reporting: where it helps and where judgement stays](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-16-ai-for-caro-2020-reporting-where-it-helps-and-where-judgement-stays); for training juniors to check tool output on both reports, see [AI and articleship](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-15-ai-and-articleship-how-ca-firms-should-train-article-assistants-now).

## Frequently asked questions

### When does Form 26 replace Form 3CD?

Form No. 26 applies for tax years beginning on or after 1 April 2026, under section 63 of the Income-tax Act, 2025. Forms 3CA, 3CB and 3CD continue for tax audits relating to assessment years up to 2026-27.

### Can AI fill in a tax audit report?

It can prepare the data and propose answers for review, which is where most of the time goes. The clause answers, the categorisation of observations and the signature remain the accountant’s responsibility, and every proposed answer should be checked against the books before it is accepted.

### What is the tax audit threshold under the new Act?

According to the Department’s Form 26 FAQs, business turnover above ₹1 crore (₹10 crore where cash receipts and payments each stay within 5%), professional receipts above ₹50 lakh, and certain presumptive taxation cases.

### Does server location matter for tax audit now?

Yes. Form 26 asks for the IP address and country of the server holding electronic books and the address of the India-located daily backup, in line with Rule 46 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026.

# AI for Internal Audit in Indian Companies: A Practical Starting Point

> A CA's starting point for AI in internal audit in India: who s.138 covers, what ICAI's new SIA 240 on tools asks for, and one full-population test.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-08-ai-for-internal-audit-in-indian-companies-a-practical-starting-point
Last updated: 2026-10-22

CA insights · 2026-10-08 · 11 min read

A CA's starting point for AI in internal audit in India: who s.138 covers, what ICAI's new SIA 240 on tools asks for, and one full-population test.

Key takeaways

- Rule 13 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, under section 138, requires an internal auditor in listed companies and in unlisted public and private companies above set turnover or borrowing thresholds.
- ICAI's SIA 240 expects tools, including AI, to be validated and documented, and says the internal auditor should not rely solely on automated outputs.
- Start with full-population testing of one high-volume process, such as procure-to-pay, instead of a sample.
- AI helps turn policy into tests, draft code, group exceptions and draft observations; people decide what is an issue and sign the report.
- Under CARO 2020 clause 3(xiv), the statutory auditor reports on whether the internal audit system is commensurate with the business.

If you run internal audit in an Indian company, or your CA firm is the appointed internal auditor under section 138, here is my short answer on AI: do not start with a dashboard. Start by testing one high-volume process on the full population instead of a sample, let people investigate every exception the test throws up, and document the tool the way you would document any other audit procedure. ICAI has now written that expectation down in a standard of its own, which makes this a good year to begin properly.

I trained as a Chartered Accountant, spent my early years in Big 4 assurance, and now help finance and audit teams put AI into real workflows. The pattern I see in internal audit is the same one I saw in statutory audit: the technology is rarely the constraint. Clean data, a clear test and a reviewer who knows the business are.

## Who this applies to: section 138 and Rule 13

Internal audit is not optional for a large part of corporate India. [Rule 13 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014](https://thc.nic.in/Central%20Governmental%20Rules/Companies%20%28Accounts%29%20Rules,%202014..pdf), made under section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013, requires an internal auditor in:

- every listed company;
- every unlisted public company with paid-up share capital of ₹50 crore or more, turnover of ₹200 crore or more, outstanding loans or borrowings from banks or public financial institutions above ₹100 crore, or outstanding deposits of ₹25 crore or more, at any point in the preceding financial year;
- every private company with turnover of ₹200 crore or more, or outstanding loans or borrowings from banks or public financial institutions above ₹100 crore, at any point in the preceding financial year.

Two details in the rule matter for AI. First, the internal auditor can be a Chartered Accountant, whether or not in practice, or an employee of the company, so the function may sit with an in-house team or an outside firm. Second, the Audit Committee or the Board, in consultation with the internal auditor, formulates the scope, functioning, periodicity and methodology of the internal audit. Moving from sampling to full-population analytics is a change of methodology. Take it to the Audit Committee before you rely on it, not after.

## What the standards now say about tools and AI

ICAI's Internal Audit Standards Board issued a [revised compendium of Standards on Internal Audit in 2026](https://internalaudit.icai.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Comp-of-Stnd-on-Internal-Audit-26.pdf). It rationalises the earlier standards into 20 SIAs and adds new ones, including **SIA 240, Use of Tools**. SIA 240 names data analytics platforms, CAATs, visualisation tools, audit management software and "emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML)". It is recommendatory and effective from 1 April 2026 until the ICAI Council notifies the date from which it applies to internal audits.

The requirements read like a sensible AI policy. Paraphrasing paragraph 4:

- **Plan it.** Evaluate and record the proposed use of tools at the planning stage, aligned to the risk assessment.
- **Validate it.** Check tools for relevance, reliability, security and confidentiality, and confirm that outputs are complete and accurate. The application material suggests trial runs, benchmarking against known outcomes and cross-checks with manual procedures.
- **Protect the data.** Tools must comply with data privacy and cybersecurity rules, and third-party tools need confidentiality, ownership and access controls. The standard names the DPDP Act, 2023.
- **Document it.** Record the rationale, configuration, test parameters and outcomes, and disclose any limitation that affects the conclusion.
- **Keep judgement.** "The internal auditor should not rely solely on automated outputs."

The same compendium carries SIA 230 on internal audit evidence and SIA 250 on documentation, so an AI-assisted test is held to the same evidence and file standard as a manual one. Internationally, the [IIA Global Internal Audit Standards](https://www.theiia.org/en/standards/), with 15 principles across five domains, [took effect on 9 January 2025](https://www.theiia.org/en/content/communications/press-releases/2025/january/the-iia-celebrates-the-effective-date-of-the-global-internal-audit-standards/), and Standard 10.3 deals with the technological resources a function needs. If your team follows both frameworks, the direction is the same.

## Where internal audit actually is with AI

It is earlier than the conference talks suggest. The IIA's [2025 North American Pulse of Internal Audit](https://www.theiia.org/globalassets/site/resources/research-and-reports/pulse-of-internal-audit/2025-iia-pulse-report.pdf) found that the share of chief audit executives using generative AI rose from 15% in the previous edition to 40%. In the same survey, 92% named data analytics as the most important technology skill for internal audit, yet only 28% described their own analytics use as high or advanced. The IIA's [Vision 2035 research](https://www.theiia.org/globalassets/site/foundation/latest-research-and-products/vision-2035-report.pdf) reported that 18% of respondents were using AI in internal audit and a further 22% were researching it.

Those surveys lean heavily towards North America, and I have not seen a comparable Indian dataset, so treat them as direction rather than benchmark. But the gap they show matches what I see: teams want generative AI, and many have not yet built the analytics habits that make it useful. Finance more broadly is similar. [Gartner's 2025 AI in Finance survey](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-11-18-gartner-survey-shows-finance-ai-adoption-remains-steady-in-2025) found 59% of finance functions using AI, with error and anomaly detection among the three most common use cases.

## Start with full-population testing of one process

Sampling exists because testing everything used to be expensive. It is not any more. If a process produces structured data, a script can test every transaction, and the conversation with the audit committee changes from "we found nothing in 25 samples" to "we tested all of them, and here are the exceptions we investigated."

Good first candidates are processes with volume, clear rules and data you can extract from the ERP:

- **Procure-to-pay:** duplicate invoices, vendor master changes close to payment runs, purchase orders split to stay under an approval limit, payments to vendors who share bank details or addresses with employees.
- **Employee expenses:** claims on non-working days, repeated round amounts, the same receipt claimed twice, claims approved by the claimant's own reportee.
- **Payroll:** employees sharing bank accounts, pay to people after their exit date, changes to pay made outside the approval workflow.
- **Revenue and receivables:** credit notes raised shortly after period end, manual adjustments to customer balances, discounts outside the policy grid.

Pick one. The temptation to build a "continuous auditing platform" in the first quarter is strong and, in my experience, the reason many analytics programmes stall.

## Where AI helps, and where it must not decide

Most full-population testing is plain analytics: joins, filters and rules. AI earns its place around that core, and SIA 240's examples (Python scripts and AI-based applications alongside IDEA, ACL and Power BI) fit how I would use it:

- **Turning policy into tests.** Give an assistant the delegation-of-authority matrix or the travel policy and ask it to propose test rules. The auditor approves every rule before it runs.
- **Writing the code.** AI is good at drafting the SQL or Python for a test. Someone who can read it still reviews it, and the reviewed version is what goes on file.
- **Grouping exceptions.** When a test returns hundreds of hits, AI can cluster them by vendor, approver or pattern so the team investigates causes rather than rows.
- **Drafting observations.** A first draft of the finding, the risk and the recommendation, which the auditor then rewrites in the company's language and rates.

What stays human: deciding whether an exception is a real issue, the conversation with the process owner, the risk rating, the conclusion and the report. SIA 240's application material says anomalies flagged by tools should be followed up through sampling, walkthroughs or corroborative procedures. That is the line I would draw.

## A six-step way to run the first test

- **1. Scope it with the Audit Committee.** One process, one period, a stated objective, and a note that the methodology is changing to full-population testing.
- **2. Get the data and prove it is complete.** Extract the transactions and agree control totals to the ledger before you test anything. A brilliant test on an incomplete extract is worthless evidence.
- **3. Write and validate the tests.** Draft rules from the policy (AI can help), then run them against a period where you already know the answer, which is the "benchmarking against known outcomes" SIA 240 describes.
- **4. Run on the full population.** Keep the scripts, parameters and output files versioned.
- **5. Investigate exceptions.** People do this. Record what was checked, what the process owner said and what evidence closed each item.
- **6. Report and document.** Report what was tested and what was found, including any limits of the data, and put the tool documentation on file as SIA 240 and SIA 250 expect.

## Controls around the AI itself

Internal audit asks everyone else for controls, so its own AI use should be the best-controlled in the building. My minimum set:

- **Approved tools only.** Company or firm-controlled accounts with retention and training settings you have checked, never personal chatbot accounts. Payroll and vendor data contain personal data.
- **Know your data-protection exposure.** The [DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified in November 2025](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2190014) with an 18-month phased timeline, and [the Act allows penalties of up to ₹250 crore](https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/nov/doc20251117695301.pdf) for failing to maintain reasonable security safeguards. Share the minimum fields a test needs.
- **A tool register.** Which tools, which versions, who may use them, for what. SIA 240 suggests a centralised tool registry, version control and usage logs.
- **No unreviewed output in the report.** Every AI-drafted rule, script and observation has a named reviewer.

For a broader version of these review gates, see my [AI controls checklist for CA firms in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-controls-checklist-ca-firms-india).

## Remember who reads the file next

Internal audit work does not stay inside the company. Under [CARO 2020](https://taxguru.in/company-law/caro-2020.html), clause 3(xiv) asks the statutory auditor whether the company has an internal audit system commensurate with its size and the nature of its business, and whether the internal auditors' reports for the period were considered. If your exceptions list came from an undocumented prompt, expect questions. If it came from a validated, versioned test with a clear trail of investigation, you have made the statutory auditor's job easier, and your own position stronger.

This is also where internal audit differs from statutory audit. For the statutory side, with SA 230 documentation, read [AI for audit working papers in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-30-ai-for-audit-working-papers-in-india-what-a-ca-should-automate-and-what-must-stay-human). For how firms are adopting AI more generally, read [how audit and accounting firms in India are using AI](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-how-audit-and-accounting-firms-in-india-are-using-ai).

## What I would tell an Audit Committee

- We will test one process on the full population this quarter, not a sample.
- Every exception will be investigated by a person, and the file will show how each one was closed.
- The tools, scripts and AI assistance will be documented in line with SIA 240, and no client or employee data will go into unapproved tools.
- We will report what the data could and could not tell us.
- If it works, we will extend it to a second process next quarter. If it does not, we will say why.

If you want a structured way to choose that first process and run it, my [90-day AI pilot playbook](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-07-how-to-run-a-90-day-ai-pilot-in-a-ca-firm-in-india) applies just as well to an internal audit team. The wider picture for the profession is in the [AI for Chartered Accountants in India hub](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/ai-for-chartered-accountants-in-india). If you would rather have someone map where AI pays back across your finance and audit work, that is what the [AI Opportunity Audit](https://pratikbajoria.com/audit) is for.

## The statutory audit side

Statutory auditors face the same tool questions on CARO 2020, where most clauses are evidence assembly followed by a judgement; I go through it clause by clause in [AI for CARO 2020 reporting: where it helps and where judgement stays](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-16-ai-for-caro-2020-reporting-where-it-helps-and-where-judgement-stays). For what SA 230 still demands of the file whoever drafted it, see [AI for audit working papers in India](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-09-30-ai-for-audit-working-papers-in-india-what-a-ca-should-automate-and-what-must-stay-human), and for training juniors to check tool output, [AI and articleship](https://pratikbajoria.com/blog/2026-10-15-ai-and-articleship-how-ca-firms-should-train-article-assistants-now).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is internal audit mandatory for my company in India?

Section 138 of the Companies Act, 2013, read with Rule 13 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014, requires an internal auditor in every listed company; in unlisted public companies with paid-up share capital of ₹50 crore or more, turnover of ₹200 crore or more, outstanding borrowings above ₹100 crore or deposits of ₹25 crore or more; and in private companies with turnover of ₹200 crore or more or outstanding borrowings above ₹100 crore. Check the thresholds against your own preceding-year figures.

### Do ICAI's Standards on Internal Audit allow AI?

Yes. SIA 240, Use of Tools, in ICAI's 2026 compendium names AI and machine learning alongside data analytics and CAATs. It asks the internal auditor to plan and record tool use, validate tool outputs for completeness and accuracy, protect data, document configurations and results, and not rely solely on automated outputs. It is recommendatory from 1 April 2026 until the ICAI Council notifies a mandatory date.

### What is the best first AI use case for an internal audit team?

In my view, full-population testing of one high-volume process, such as procure-to-pay or employee expense claims. It replaces sampling with a complete test, the exceptions are easy to verify, and it fits the evidence and documentation requirements the team already follows.

### Does the statutory auditor look at internal audit work?

Yes. Under CARO 2020, clause 3(xiv), the statutory auditor reports whether the company has an internal audit system commensurate with its size and nature, and whether the internal auditors' reports were considered. AI-assisted work therefore needs to be documented well enough for another auditor to follow.

### Will AI replace internal auditors?

No. It changes the work. Testing every transaction becomes cheap; deciding which exceptions matter, talking to process owners, rating findings and standing behind the report still need an experienced person. SIA 240 says as much: tool findings need professional scepticism and contextual evaluation.

# Privacy in plain English.

> Privacy notice for pratikbajoria.com: what the discovery-call, cross-border and newsletter forms store, who can see it, and how to ask for deletion.

Canonical: https://pratikbajoria.com/privacy
Last updated: 2026-09-18

When you submit a discovery-call request or a cross-border partnership enquiry, or subscribe to the AI Implementation Brief, this site stores the information you provide — such as your name, email, company, phone number and message — in a private Cloudflare D1 database so Pratik can respond and manage the relationship.

Access to submissions is restricted to the site owner. The site does not sell your information. Information may be shared with a service provider only when needed to operate the website or respond to you. You can request access, correction or deletion by emailing [hello@pratikbajoria.com](mailto:hello@pratikbajoria.com).

WhatsApp and email buttons open your chosen external service with a pre-filled message. Their handling of information is governed by their own privacy policies. Affiliate partners may use cookies or tracking parameters when you follow a disclosed link.

To understand how the site is used, pages load Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity after the page has displayed. They record anonymised usage such as pages viewed, clicks, scrolling and, in Clarity's case, heatmaps and session replays; form fields are masked and no names, emails or form text are sent to them. Microsoft's handling is described in the [Microsoft Privacy Statement](https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement).

The voice agent uses your browser's speech recognition and speech synthesis capabilities after you press the microphone button. This website does not store your audio or transcript; browser speech processing may be handled by your browser provider.

This concise notice should be reviewed with the final email provider, analytics configuration and applicable Indian privacy obligations before a paid acquisition campaign or large-scale email programme launches.
